title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract:
Abstract
                  Deforestation is a major source of global greenhouse gas emissions, and continued forest loss risks pushing the Amazon from a carbon sink to a carbon source. While recent work shows that productivity-led structural transformation towards less land-intensive sectors can reduce deforestation, the labour market implications of such pathways remain poorly understood. Here we address this gap by developing a spatially and occupationally explicit agent-based labour market model informed by empirically observed job-transition networks to simulate the ability of workers to respond to labour demand shocks. Our analysis reveals significant skill and geographic mobility frictions that constrain workers’ ability to adapt to structural change. Applying the model to productivity-driven development scenarios, we find that pathways delivering the largest deforestation and emission reductions disproportionately benefit high-skill workers while increasing unemployment among agricultural and other low-skill workers. Mobility-enhancing labour market policies can mitigate these effects, highlighting the importance of understanding labour market dynamics for equitable and feasible deforestation-reducing development pathways.

title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract:
Abstract
                  Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. We combine integrated assessment models, climate projections, economic damage functions and biosphere datasets to assess asset changes under multiple mitigation scenarios. Geopolitical challenges and opportunities arise from climate change mitigation because losses and gains across energy and environmental assets are country-specific, which we further characterize through a broad clustering and a detailed pairwise similarity analysis. Our analysis suggests comparatively moderate impacts for the USA, the European Union and China, highlighting the challenge that the largest economic powers may not be those with the strongest asset-based interest for climate action. While our framework remains limited, our data provide input for integrating other ethical, governance and socioeconomic factors in future analyses of opportunities and challenges for ambitious climate change mitigation.

title: Operando resolution of CO2 electrolysis interfaces at application-relevant current density reveals water gating
source: Nature Catalysis
abstract: Design of CO2 electroreduction (CO2R) interfaces requires understanding of the dynamic interplay among reactants, surface species and ions. Simplified ideal frameworks, which are conventionally employed to identify these dependencies, provide limited insights under relevant conditions. Here we resolve species interplay in membrane electrode assemblies up to high current densities (1 A cm−2), combining operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics. We identify a key role of water ordering in regulation of access to the interface along different operation regimes. Initially, double-layer water exhibits a dominant four-hydrogen-bond (4-HB) coordination with a random configuration. With increasing current density, water rearranges to a three-hydrogen-bond coordination and sits H-down close to the surface, acting as the primary proton source for CO2R and generating adsorbed hydroxides. Eventually, this results in carbonate build-up that increases the concentration of H-down 4-HB water, restricting interface access to COx reactants and promoting hydrogen evolution. These results increase our understanding of CO2R interfaces up to application-relevant current densities. Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. Here operando Raman spectroscopy is used in combination with molecular dynamics simulations to establish the role of water ordering in the mechanism of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction over a range of current densities and under practical conditions.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Programming hierarchical helicity from molecular stereochemistry remains a major challenge in synthetic materials. Collagen achieves this through conformational preorganization that translates local stereochemical information into homochiral triple helices, a level of hierarchical control rarely realized in artificial systems. Here we show that atomically precise Au4 nanoclusters encode local stereochemical information into a homochiral triple helix through a collagen-inspired assembly mechanism. A configuration-dependent endo-exo puckering of thiazolidine-2-thione ligands acts as a stereochemical switch, controlling metal-site exposure and biasing Au···Au metallophilic interactions. This intrachain preorganization fixes the torsional geometry of single helices, which then cooperatively braid into left-handed and right-handed triple helices, respectively. Systematic steric modulation redirects the assembly into alternative architectures, demonstrating programmable control over helicity. The triple-helical superstructures exhibit amplified chiroptical responses. These results establish a transferable molecular grammar for hierarchical helicity in metal nanoclusters and identify metallophilicity as a design principle for biomimetic materials.

title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
source: Nature Climate Change
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample (
                    N
                     = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted.

title: Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators operating at gigahertz frequencies are a promising platform for quantum information processing and precision sensing, but phonon lifetimes have been limited to the microsecond range, widely attributed to the higher intrinsic loss of piezoelectric materials. Here we show that this limitation is not fundamental. Using a fabrication process informed by recent studies of defect-mediated loss in lithium niobate, we combine the chemical restoration of ion-milled surfaces with a shadow-mask metallization process to produce lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with inferred internal phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at 3.6 GHz, corresponding to quality factors exceeding 4 × 108 (f × Qi > 1018) at millikelvin temperatures. By systematically varying the electrode-to-resonator spacing, we demonstrate that the measured lifetime is set by external coupling between the device and measurement circuit rather than material loss. This establishes that lithium niobate, once fabrication-induced surface damage is removed, achieves an intrinsic quality comparable with the best mechanical materials while remaining an intrinsically piezoelectric platform with strong electromechanical coupling.

title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: The generation of unidirectional motion has been a long-standing challenge in the engineering of molecular motors and, more generally, machines. A molecular motor is characterized by a set of low-energy states that differ in their configuration, that is, position or rotation. In biology and Feringa-type motors, unidirectional motion is driven by excitation of the molecule into a high-energy transitional state followed by a directional relaxation back to a low-energy state. Directionality is created by a steric hindrance to movement along one of the directions on the path from the excited state back to a low-energy state. Here we showcase a principal mechanism for the generation of unidirectional rotation of a molecule without the need for steric hindrance and transitional excited states. The chemical design of the molecule-consisting of a platform, an upright axle and a chiral rotor moiety-enables a rotation mechanism that relies on the transfer of orbital angular momentum from the driving current to the rotor. The transfer is mediated via orbital currents that are carried by helical orbitals in the axle.

title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Metal-free molecular magnets differ from conventional magnetic devices that predominantly rely on metallic magnets as these metal-free materials may offer biocompatibility and bioresorbability. However, existing molecular materials lack the ferromagnetic strength required for high-fidelity sensing at clinically relevant tissue depths. Here we introduce a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet derived from graphitic carbon nitride, combining metallic-level ferromagnetism with full bioresorbability. De-nitrogenation creates spin centres coupled through a reconstructed π-σ conjugated framework, conferring robust spontaneous magnetization that remains stable under physiological conditions. Integrated with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and silk fibroin, the material forms catheter-deliverable epicardial patches for cardiac tracking and can also be dispersed in injectable hydrogels for organ-scale sensing, including the three-dimensional reconstruction of localized hepatic pathologies. Coupled with a skin-interfaced Hall array, this magnetic sensing architecture provides the continuous, untethered monitoring of multi-organ dynamics, robust against motion artifacts and tissue impedance. In porcine models, it facilitates the continuous assessment of ejection fraction over 4 weeks, followed by benign bioresorption. Benchmarked against standard-of-care echocardiography, this approach delivers clinical-grade trajectories, supporting longitudinal, infrastructure-independent physiological monitoring.

title: Elevating CO2 electrolyzer temperature accelerates the viability of chemical electrification
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change mitigation has spurred interest in producing chemicals from CO

However, the resulting processes still suffer from high electrolyzer losses and substantial energy demands. This study evaluates the environmental and economic benefits of integrating optimized electrolyzers into complete processes. For CO

title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes
source: Nature
abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)–Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs–Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs–Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·–, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs–Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs–Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs–Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs–Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core–shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

title: In Situ Tracking of Se Vacancy-Promoted Surface Reconstruction of NiCoSe2 into NiCoOOH during Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding the dynamic surface reconstruction of precatalyst materials during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a forefront area of research for designing and studying effective electrocatalysts. Here, we report the deliberate engineering of Se vacancies in NiCoSe2 via a facile NaBH4 reduction strategy and systematically investigate how anion vacancies govern surface reconstruction behavior under alkaline OER conditions. The presence of Se vacancies is confirmed via EPR spectroscopy and ICP-MS analysis. Cyclic voltammetry and in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy during the electrochemical activation process reveal that the vacancy-enriched NiCoSe2–x undergoes faster and more extensive structural reconstruction than pristine NiCoSe2. Quasi in situ ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy track the dynamic evolution of NiCoOOH during anodic polarization, providing direct spectroscopic evidence for the Se vacancy-promoted NiCoOOH active phase generation with abundant Ni–O–Co synergy. Evaluation of electrochemical surface area and turnover frequency establishes that the generation of abundant Ni–O–Co synergy in NiCoSe2–x simultaneously increases the density of accessible active sites and enhances the intrinsic activity per site. Consequently, the NiCoSe2–x precatalyst delivers significantly improved OER performance relative to bare NiCoSe2, along with high Faradaic selectivity and long-term stability. Post-stability characterizations confirm bulk structural and morphological reconstruction driven by Se vacancies and thus highlight the complete utilization of the available catalytic sites. This work provides a fundamental mechanistic framework linking anion vacancy engineering, surface reconstruction kinetics/mechanism tracking, and intrinsic OER activity enhancement in bimetallic chalcogenide precatalysts, offering rationalized design principles for next-generation earth-abundant OER catalysts.

title: Three-Dimensional Crosslinked CNT/SiO x -F Network Encapsulated by Pitch-Derived Carbon as a High-Stable Anode for Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Intrinsic low conductivity and huge volume expansion severely limit the cycling stability of SiOx anodes. Herein, a 3D crosslinked CNT/SiOx-F@C composite is synthesized via bifunctional fluorosilane crosslinkers and conformal pitch carbon coating. Fluorosilane acts as both a silicon source and a crosslinker to build interconnected, conductive CNT frameworks, while the outer pitch carbon optimizes the pore structure and induces flexible, LixPOyF6-rich SEI layers. Kinetic tests reveal dominant capacitive charge storage and a Li+ diffusion coefficient one-order-of-magnitude higher than that of control electrodes. The half-cell delivers a stable reversible capacity of 672.6 mA h g–1 over 200 cycles at 0.2 A g–1 and retains 86.5% capacity after 600 cycles at 1 A g–1. Pre-lithiation elevates the initial Coulombic efficiency from 47.4 to 84.2%, while the electrode achieves an areal capacity approaching 4 mA h cm–2, far exceeding that of commercial graphite. This dual-carbon synergistic strategy provides a facile route to optimizing silicon oxide anodes.

title: Hydrogel Microneedle-Enabled In Situ Monitoring of Leaf Nitric Oxide for Evaluating NO Nanoprodrug-Mediated Salt Stress Alleviation in Maize
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chemical signals in living plants are spatially confined, rapidly consumed, and strongly dependent on the delivery history of exogenous regulators, creating a need for bioelectronic interfaces that can interrogate molecular dynamics directly within intact tissues. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) nanoprodrug with a conductive hydrogel microneedle platform to connect controlled molecular delivery, in planta electrochemical readout, and downstream biological responses in living maize. The working electrode comprises a poly(vinyl alcohol)/aramid nanofiber (PVA/ANF) hydrogel containing FeMo-N/C and an MXene conductive network. The hydrated microneedle architecture provides tissue-conformal contact and analyte transport, FeMo-N/C enhances the NO-associated electrochemical response, and MXene improves interfacial charge transfer. The resulting platform responds to NO from 1 nM to 100 μM with a detection limit of 0.3 nM and discriminates NO from representative electroactive plant interferents. Chitosan nanoparticles containing S-nitroso-mercaptosuccinic acid were used to moderate NO release, and the microneedle interface resolved treatment-dependent leaf signals over 7 days under salt stress. Signal attenuation by the NO scavenger cPTIO supported the NO-related origin of the electrochemical response. The time-resolved readout was accompanied by improved growth, reduced lipid peroxidation, changes in osmotic and antioxidant responses, and altered expression of stress-responsive genes. This delivery–bioelectronics–analysis framework provides a materials-based strategy for evaluating reactive nanoprodrugs and interrogating transient chemical signaling in living plants.

title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800–5050 nm and width: 780–970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst’s analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

title: Regiocontrolled One-Step Indole Synthesis from Carbonyl Compounds via Organobismuth Chemistry
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Indoles are privileged scaffolds in natural products, pharmaceuticals, and synthetic intermediates, and their concise, regioselective synthesis remains an enduring challenge. Here, we report a one-step indole synthesis enabled by 2-aminophenyl-tBuBisTrip (aryl–BisTrip) (2), a bismuth(V) reagent that effects rapid α-arylation of lithium enolates followed by spontaneous annulation. The method is effective for a wide range of cyclic and acyclic ketones, including challenging cyclopentanones and heterocyclic substrates, as well as 1,2- and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds and enolates derived from silyl enol ethers. Notably, the platform enables direct indole annulation of enones, a substrate class that has remained problematic via Fischer or transition-metal-catalyzed methods. The utility of the transformation is further illustrated by late-stage indole installation on complex bioactive molecules and by a desymmetrization sequence that translates asymmetric deprotonation into chiral indole synthesis. Together, these results establish a general main-group-enabled approach for regiocontrolled indole construction from simple carbonyl precursors.

title: High-Mobility a-InZnO Thin-Film Transistors Incorporating an Oxygen-Related Defect Control Layer for Improved Illumination Stability and Environmental Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The introduction of an appropriate passivation layer is considered a viable strategy for improving the long-term stability and electrical performance of thin-film transistors (TFTs). In this study, an additional layer deposition strategy involving the deposition of a single-layer oxygen-related defect control layer on amorphous indium zinc oxide (a-IZO) thin-film transistors is developed. This approach improves the electrical characteristics and negative-bias illumination stress (NBIS) stability of the channel layer. The oxygen-related defect control layer is a hafnium oxynitride (HfON) layer. It functions as an insulating material with a relatively high dielectric constant, high film density, and low surface energy, serving as a protective barrier against environmental degradation such as exposure to ambient air and moisture. In addition, it contributes to the improvement of NBIS-induced stability by passivating the defect sites in a-IZO during the activation annealing process. Furthermore, the number of carriers in the channel layer increased because of the formation of oxygen vacancies in the a-IZO front channel through the oxygen adsorption of the oxygen-related defect control layer, resulting in the fabrication of thin films with better electrical properties. This resulted in field-effect mobility improving from 37.53 to 66.43 cm2/(V s), the on/off current ratio was enhanced from 1.93 × 109 to 5.77 × 1011, and the threshold voltage shift under NBIS at green light (532 nm) flux density of 1 mW/cm2 for 10,000 s decreased from 15.25 to 2.64 V.

title: A comprehensive review of global advanced metering infrastructure cost-benefit evidence and a data-integration framework for master-metered high-voltage apartment complexes
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) is the core sensing layer of decarbonizing grids, but its value is realized only where interval data reach the grid operator and the tariff setter. This review synthesizes three separate literatures: the functional evolution of metering; cross-national AMI cost-benefit analyses (CBAs) covering Europe, Japan and South Korea; and data governance in master-metered multi-occupancy buildings. Deconstructing CBA formulations shows that only labor substitution accrues directly from meter installation; every other benefit category depends on coefficients that require data reachability. This helps account for the order-of-magnitude dispersion in benefit–cost ratios, which is associated more closely with the evaluation boundary and complementary institutions than with technology cost, and exposes a structural vulnerability in South Korea. Deployment reached 20 million low-voltage customers in 2024 (B/C 1.03), yet the 11.96 million households in 28,253 high-voltage apartment complexes largely sit outside the metering data pipeline: the complex, not the household, is the contracting customer, and household meters are private assets behind the supply point. AMI hardware reaches 53% of these households but only 15.4% (1.84 million) are linked to the utility, leaving 4.5 million households whose interval data reach a private server and go no further. The exclusion became binding in 2026, when residential time-of-use (TOU) tariffs were deferred nationally for want of AMI coverage. Japan’s Specified Metering (IoT-route) system, Australia’s embedded networks and North American master metering show that such arrangements can be made useful without dissolving supply contracts. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating architecture for an apartment-dedicated meter data management system (APT-MDMS) with gateway-based integration, server-side TOU settlement, a consent and privacy architecture, and a five-year, four-segment roadmap. The proposed architecture and roadmap are design hypotheses whose system interfaces, reliability, costs and economic viability require pilot validation.

title: Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized nano-silica (modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and propyltrimethoxysilane) during prepolymerization. This strategy established an organic–inorganic interpenetrating cross-linked network through covalent bonding and intermolecular interactions. The silica nanoparticles act as interfacial bridges between polymer segments, mitigating phase separation and agglomeration caused by polarity mismatch, thereby enhancing coating compactness and improving stress transfer. Performance tests demonstrate that the properties of the coating have been comprehensively enhanced. The coating exhibits an elongation at break of 254.64% while maintaining a tensile strength of 21.17 MPa. Additionally, the water absorption rate of the coating decreases to approximately 5%, the electrochemical protection efficiency reaches 99.9920%, and no obvious corrosion phenomenon is observed after a 7 day salt spray corrosion test. Additionally, the coating shows excellent drag-reduction performance, with a drag-reduction rate of 6.56% under turbulent flow. By integrating interfacial design with nanocomposite architecture, this work develops a robust WPU coating system suitable for marine engineering applications, and employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the microscopic mechanism by which amino and n-propyl silane dual modification inhibits the aggregation of silica nanoparticles as well as the interfacial interaction mechanism, thereby highlighting the role of colloidal and nanomaterial strategies in advancing functional protective coatings.
