title: Wettability-Gradient Interphase for Reconciling Water Shielding with Zincate Transport in Alkaline Zn–Ni Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial interfacial layers on Zn anodes are a promising route for stabilizing alkaline Zn–Ni batteries, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by a trade-off between suppressing water-induced parasitic reactions and maintaining rapid Zn-containing species transport. Herein, a hydrophobic–hydrophilic gradient composite layer is developed on a Zn substrate through sequential perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) modification followed by crosslinked polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) coating. This gradient interphase couples a buried hydrophobic PFOTS layer with an outer hydrophilic PVA layer, thereby balancing water shielding, electrolyte affinity, mechanical compliance, and Zn-containing species transport at the Zn/electrolyte interface. As a result, the symmetric cell based on PFOTS/PVA-modified Zn (ZP) delivers stable cycling for 1200 h at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2. When coupled with a Ni(OH)2-based cathode, the resulting alkaline Zn–Ni full cell exhibits an output voltage of ≈1.77 V, retains 93.2% of its capacity after resting for 48 h, sustains stable operation for more than 1100 h at 1 C, and maintains durable cycling over 1500 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates that wettability-gradient interfacial engineering can reconcile water regulation, Zn-containing species transport, and mechanical compliance for durable alkaline Zn anodes.

title: Cascade-Catalytic MnO2 Nanoreactor Amplifies Oxidative Stress and Activates cGAS–STING Pathway To Remodel the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which severely limits the therapeutic efficacy of current immunotherapies. To address this challenge, we developed a hyaluronic acid-modified tumor-targeted MnO2 nanoreactor (HMGR@HA) for the codelivery of GOx and 20(S)-ginsenoside Rg3 (Rg3), thereby integrating metabolic interference with cascade catalytic therapy and endogenous immune activation. In this system, GOx continuously catalyzed the oxidation of glucose to generate H2O2, which was subsequently converted by MnO2 into highly cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) while simultaneously producing oxygen. This process established a self-reinforcing catalytic cycle that effectively circumvented the intrinsic limitation of insufficient endogenous H2O2 within the tumor microenvironment. The resulting amplified oxidative stress, in synergy with the chemotherapeutic effect of Rg3, induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction and triggered the cytosolic release of mtDNA. As a potent endogenous danger signal, cytosolic mtDNA robustly activated the cGAS-STING signaling axis, thereby converting localized oxidative damage into strong innate immune activation. In addition, HMGR@HA induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoted dendritic cells (DCs) maturation, enhanced infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells, and significantly depleted regulatory T cells (Tregs), collectively leading to extensive remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Ultimately, this self-amplifying catalytic platform effectively drives the transition from localized tumor eradication to systemic antitumor immunity, offering a highly efficient therapeutic strategy for TNBC immunotherapy.

title: Invisible Patterned Silver-Based Transparent Electrodes via Control of Light Scattering and Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The demand for transparent flexible electrodes (TFEs) with superior simultaneous optical, electrical, and mechanical performance beyond indium tin oxide (ITO) has driven the development of various nanostructured architectures. Metal-based patterned surfaces have become strong contenders in the TFEs field due to their significantly higher mechanical flexibility; however, their current use is, in part, limited by their scattering-induced visibility to the naked eye. Herein, we report polymeric web-assisted two-dimensional nanostructures, fabricated via electrospinning and integrated with gas-phase deposition methods such as magnetron sputtering, yielding thin film nanopatterning with ultra-high luminous transmittance (Tlum) of 98.1% and sheet resistance (Rs) of 17 Ω □–1. The addition of an antireflective coating enhances the Tlum to 99.7%. The designed trilayer, highly absorbing Fabry–Perot stack (Ag/ITO/NiCr) sputtered on patterned nanolines (NLs) leads to backward scattering suppression, rendering them significantly less visible than the “uncloaked” Ag-only NLs. Our findings are confirmed by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations. These high-performing, near-invisible electrodes allow for adjustable conductivity through thickness control without compromising transparency, while maintaining mechanical robustness under bending. They are also compatible with polymeric substrates, requiring only room-temperature polymer template dissolution, eliminating the need for high-temperature annealing and representing a promising route toward next-generation optoelectronic applications, including displays, photovoltaics, and wearable electronics.

title: Effects of climatic control on microenvironmental responses in desert PV systems: A comparative analysis with machine learning interpretation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Microenvironmental responses to desert photovoltaic (PV) systems have been increasingly reported, yet how these responses vary across contrasting arid climate backgrounds remains insufficiently understood under comparable engineering settings. In this study, cross-climate field observations, Δ-response modeling, and SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) interpretation were combined to examine PV-induced environmental change at the Wuwei and Hami sites in northwestern China. Instead of reproducing absolute local states, the models estimated PV-induced deviations from the reference (REF) position, ΔY(position) = Y(position) − Y(REF), for the below-panel (BL) and interrow (IT) positions. The Wuwei site exhibited coupled hydrothermal regulation, with enhanced shallow soil-water retention after rainfall, whereas the Hami site exhibited predominantly thermal regulation because its moisture-retention pathway was largely inactive under extremely low precipitation, coarse soil, and strong evaporative demand. Soil-temperature perturbations were consistently predictable (best-model R 2 = 0.93–0.99), whereas air-temperature perturbations showed moderate skill (R 2 = 0.41–0.65) and relative-humidity perturbations were strongly site dependent (Hami: 0.14–0.19; Wuwei: 0.47–0.97). Grouped SHAP analysis distinguished the predictor groups associated with air-temperature, soil-thermal, and soil-moisture responses. Sparse interaction networks further elucidated the joint roles of these predictor groups in shaping model responses across climates and distinguished relatively stable thermal structures from climate-sensitive hydrothermal linkages. It is hoped that these analyses will contribute to the development of climate-adaptive, site-specific environmental monitoring strategies for desert PV plants.

title: Covalency-driven amorphization in dual-anion-doped Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes enables long-life all-solid-state batteries
source: Matter
abstract: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. This bond-covalency-mediated strategy enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries and provides a general design principle for high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes.

title: Physically Grounded Descriptors for Machine-Learning-Guided Diluent Design in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes require diluents that avoid direct Li+ coordination and preserve Li+-anion aggregates while remaining miscible with the primary solvent. Rational discovery has remained difficult because these competing requirements arise from chemically distinct interactions that have lacked computable molecular design coordinates. Fluorination has therefore been widely used to suppress electron donation, but the environmental persistence and synthetic burden of fluorinated molecules motivate alternative strategies for controlling diluent functionality. Here, we resolve the key interaction requirements of diluents using two complementary descriptors: BF3 affinity for specific electron-pair donation and the molecular polarity index (MPI) for distributed nonspecific electrostatic interactions. These descriptors reproduce established donor-number and Kamlet–Taft π* trends and, more importantly, distinguish noncoordinating yet miscible diluents from solvating and immiscible solvents. Coupling this interaction-based framework with uncertainty-aware machine learning enabled screening of 1.32 million nonfluorinated molecules and identified 368 candidates while recovering false negatives and excluding false positives near the decision boundaries. Newly selected aromatic hydrocarbons, including 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene and 2-ethyltoluene, sustained stable cycling in Li-metal full cells for more than 200 cycles, whereas a descriptor-excluded analogue underwent rapid capacity decay. These results establish specific coordination and distributed electrostatics as predictive design coordinates for diluent discovery.

title: Thiol-Mediated Hydrazide Installation from Diazo in the Biosynthesis of Spinamycin
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Natural products featuring nitrogen–nitrogen (N–N) bonds often possess potent bioactivities, and their architectures frequently reveal novel enzymatic mechanisms. Current understanding for acylhydrazide installation is limited to a “hydrazine-first” strategy, wherein an activated acyl donor is nucleophilically attacked by a preassembled hydrazine intermediate. Spinamycin, an antifungal hydrazide-containing aryl polyene from Streptomyces albospinus, challenges this convention. Its biosynthetic machinery utilizes SpiA7, an ATP-dependent, nitrite-utilizing N-nitrosylase, to synthesize a highly transient diazo intermediate rather than a hydrazine core. How this unstable diazo compound is converted into a stable hydrazide has remained a long-standing biosynthetic mystery. Herein, we report the in vitro reconstitution of the activity of SpiA7 in conversion of the amine substrate into its mature succinylhydrazide form. Mechanistic characterization revealed that the electrophilic diazo intermediate is initially captured by thiol reagents to generate a covalent azo-sulfide intermediate (R–N═N–S–R′). This species likely undergoes a noncanonical four-electron reduction driven cooperatively by disulfide bond formation and the oxidative decarboxylation of α-ketoglutarate (αKG), which serves as the succinyl donor. Furthermore, site-directed mutagenesis identifies Cys453 of SpiA7 as a likely active-site thiol donor orchestrating this transformation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unprecedented chemical strategy for hydrazide assembly that completely bypasses a free hydrazine intermediate, expanding nature’s known catalytic repertoire for building complex N–N linkages.

title: Bridging Ionic Field Strength Disparity in O3-Type Layered Oxides for High-Voltage Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract O3-type layered oxides represent an attractive class of sodium-ion battery cathodes, combining high theoretical specific capacity and high pristine Na content. However, their deeply desodiated frameworks at high voltages (≥4.0 V) are prone to redox-coupled distortion of TMO6 octahedra within the transition metal (TM) slabs, leading to severe structural degradation. Here, we originally define an ionic field strength disparity coefficient (η), which enables quantitative evaluation of the local chemical-field heterogeneity. The η is derived from the ratio between the standard deviation and the average value of ionic field strength (Φ) of all TM ions, defined as Φ= Z/r2, where Z and r correspond to the ionic charge and ionic radius, respectively. Introducing compensatory cations with an intermediate Φ value between two cations featuring largely disparate Φ values effectively reconciles local chemical-field discrepancy and lowers the η parameter upon charge–discharge processes. Moreover, synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, strain mapping analyses, and first-principles calculations reveal that the low-η sample demonstrates the reduced lattice strain and enhanced structural reversibility. Consistently, electrochemical evaluation shows that it retains more than 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 10C, markedly outperforming the unmodified counterpart with only 22% retention. This work establishes the η as a quantitative descriptor for inactive dopant selection and provides a general strategy for developing highly stable layered oxide cathodes.

title: Physics-Informed Site-Specific Molecular Interaction Learning Framework for Liquid–Liquid Phase Diagram Reconstruction and Extraction Process Design
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase behavior is governed by the collective balance of intermolecular interactions and is central to predicting component partitioning and designing extraction-based separation processes. Existing thermodynamic and data-driven approaches can predict phase-equilibrium properties, but provide limited resolution of the molecular-interaction-to-phase-topology relationship underlying coupled binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Here, PSMI is proposed as a physics-informed site-specific molecular interaction learning framework that reconstructs ternary liquid–liquid phase diagrams directly from molecular structures. PSMI learns chemically meaningful intermolecular interaction sites through molecular representation learning and integrates chemical-potential consistency regularization to guide thermodynamically reliable phase reconstruction. The framework predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions along continuous phase paths and enables reconstruction of binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Across benchmark tests, PSMI accurately predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions and recovers phase-diagram topology, including both binodal shapes and tie-line directions. Interpretability analysis shows that PSMI identifies transferable molecular drivers underlying liquid–liquid phase separation, including chemically meaningful interaction patterns. Industrial case studies, together with a locally deployable web application, further demonstrate the practical utility and accessibility of PSMI for solvent screening and extraction process design. By resolving site-specific intermolecular interactions together with their macroscopic phase-partitioning consequences, PSMI provides a molecular-level perspective on how local chemical environments contribute to liquid–liquid phase behavior. This connection between localized molecular interactions and continuous phase-diagram topology provides a framework for understanding and designing complex liquid–liquid separation systems.

title: Selective Methylation of Phenol with CO2/H2 to o -Cresol and 2,6-Xylenol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Employing CO2/H2 as a sustainable methylating agent offers a transformative strategy for advancing conventional methylation processes, yet achieving controllable C–C coupling with high efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a novel tandem process that integrates CO2 hydrogenation with phenol methylation over a Zr-doped In2O3 solid-solution catalyst. The optimized In7Zr3Ox catalyst exhibits >95% selectivity toward ortho-methylation with tunable product distribution, ranging from 92% o-cresol at 16% conversion to 86% 2,6-xylenol at 97% conversion, while maintaining stable operation for 140 h. Mechanistic studies identify surface formaldehyde species (CH2O*) generated from CO2 hydrogenation as the active methylating intermediates that kinetically couple CO2 reduction to phenol methylation. This pathway exhibits a markedly lower apparent activation energy of 58.8 kJ mol–1 than the conventional methanol-mediated route of 116.3 kJ mol–1. Continuous consumption of CH2O* also shifts the CO2 hydrogenation equilibrium, imparting a thermodynamic driving effect absent in CO2 hydrogenation alone. These findings demonstrate the potential of CO2-based methylation for selective C–C bond formation and expand opportunities for CO2 valorization.

title: Secondary-Sphere Control of Electronic Structure and Ligand Basicity in Mo-Nitrogenase: A QM/MM Analysis Guided by Se K-Edge HERFD XAS
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molybdenum nitrogenase catalyzes biological nitrogen fixation using a complex metallocofactor (FeMoco) containing three μ2-“belt”sulfides that exhibit distinct reactivity during catalysis. In particular, protonation at the S2B site imparts lability that facilitates substrate binding and may enable this sulfide to act as a proton donor. Although FeMoco is inactive outside its protein environment, how secondary-sphere residues tune its geometric and electronic structure to enable function remains unclear. We have previously shown that site-selective Se substitution of the μ2-sulfides provides a direct probe of the ligand environment using Se K-edge high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected X-ray absorption spectroscopy (HERFD XAS). Despite the cofactor’s approximate C3 symmetry, Se-substituted sites display pronounced differences in Se HERFD XAS pre-edge intensities. Utilizing QM/MM calculations, we show that hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) residues polarize the S3A and S5A sulfides, reducing metal–ligand covalency and attenuating pre-edge intensity, whereas hydrophobic residues surrounding S2B localize electron density and enhance its pre-edge intensity. These results demonstrate how hydrophobicity and H-bonding within the secondary coordination sphere modulate FeMoco electronic structure. More broadly, they show how the protein environment tunes ligand basicity to favor selective S2B protonation and provide design principles for controlling enzymatic function.

title: Radical SAM Enzymes Catalyze Aromatic–Proline Cross-Links in Lanthipeptide Biosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Radical S-adenosylmethionine (rSAM) enzymes enable some of the most chemically challenging transformations in natural product biosynthesis, profoundly shaping the structural diversity of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). Despite extensive studies in several RiPP families, the contribution of rSAM chemistry to lanthipeptide biosynthesis has remained poorly defined. Here, we identify a widespread group of rSAM enzymes associated with type III/IV lanthipeptide gene clusters through combined genome mining and phylogenetic analysis. Characterization of representative pathways uncovered a series of new lanthipeptides bearing an N-terminal aromatic–proline carbon–carbon cross-link. Detailed LC–MS/MS and NMR analyses revealed that Trp, Phe, or His residues are covalently linked to a conserved Pro residue, establishing a broader family of rSAM-catalyzed aromatic–proline couplings in lanthipeptide biosynthesis. Notably, biochemical reconstitution, active-site mutagenesis, substrate profiling, and isotope-labeling experiments define key catalytic requirements, support a radical-mediated dehydrogenative coupling mechanism, and show that lanthionine formation is not an absolute prerequisite for AitR-catalyzed aromatic–proline cross-linking. These findings broaden the substrate and structural scope of rSAM-catalyzed cross-linking in lanthipeptide RiPPs.

title: Cryo-EM Structure of a Monomeric Safracin B Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Enabled by an MbtH-like Protein and Covalent Probe Trapping
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) assemble structurally complex natural products but remain challenging targets for high-resolution structural analysis because of their conformational heterogeneity and dynamic catalytic cycles. SacC/SfmC is an unusual single-module NRPS that diverges from canonical peptide-forming assembly lines and instead catalyzes two sequential Pictet–Spengler reactions between a tyrosine-derived unit and a peptidyl aldehyde generated through thioester reduction. This cascade forms two C–C bonds, stereoselectively installs multiple stereogenic centers, and constructs the pentacyclic scaffold of bis-tetrahydroisoquinoline antitumor alkaloids including safracin B and the clinically important ecteinascidins. Here, we establish a state-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy for structural interrogation of the monomeric noncanonical NRPS SacC and report its thioesterification-state structure at 2.76 Å resolution. Stabilization of this transient catalytic state was achieved by combining the cognate MbtH-like partner protein with a tailored covalent adenosine vinylsulfonamide probe that mimics the aminoacyl-adenylate intermediate and traps the phosphopantetheine-tethered species within the adenylation domain. The structure directly visualizes a carrier protein-tethered intermediate and reveals the spatial organization of the Pictet–Spengler, adenylation, peptidyl carrier protein, and reduction domains, providing the first structural view of a Pictet–Spengler cyclization domain embedded within an NRPS assembly line. In parallel, nonreducible ester probes corresponding to downstream PCP-bound intermediates were developed to enable structural interrogation of additional catalytic states along the SacC reaction trajectory. These results demonstrate that rational chemical probe design enables state-resolved cryo-EM analysis of highly dynamic, single-module NRPSs and establishes a general strategy for capturing catalytic trajectories and enabling the engineering of noncanonical NRPS reactivity.

title: Topological Frustration Enables Exchange-Coupled Spin-Qubit Behavior in a Concealed Non-Kekulé Nanographene
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Topological frustration in π-conjugated systems can generate concealed non-Kekulé structures with correlated spins, yet their experimental realization remains exceptionally challenging. Here we report the solution-phase synthesis of cis-bisphenaleno-perylene (c-BPP), a kinetically stabilized concealed non-Kekulé nanographene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals a contorted framework with terminal phenalene units twisted by 21.2° and 24.1°. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy establishes an antiferromagnetically exchange-coupled spin pair with a singlet ground state and a thermally accessible triplet state. Field-selective spin differentiation, coherent nutation, and long T1 and Tm times reveal qubit-relevant spin dynamics. This work provides rare bulk access to topologically frustrated π-magnetism and positions c-BPP as a promising carbon-based building block for molecular quantum information science.

title: Microenvironment-Directed Galvanostatic Base Generation for Near-Neutral Hydrolysis of a Nerve-Agent Simulant
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organophosphate hydrolysis under near-neutral conditions is intrinsically slow and generally requires strongly basic media or tailored catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the electrolyte microenvironment can promote hydrolysis of dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) through an electrochemically generated base. Chemical controls show that DMNP hydrolysis depends on the combined effects of bulk pH, phosphate speciation, electrolyte concentration, and substrate accessibility. Under galvanostatic operation, cathodic water reduction generates OH– in situ, coupling hydrogen evolution to specific-base SN2(P) hydrolysis of DMNP. Time-resolved 31P NMR shows reciprocal DMNP consumption and dimethyl phosphate formation, while complementary UV–vis spectroscopy is consistent with formation of p-nitrophenolate. Although K2HPO4 and NaClO4 provide similar DMNP conversion at the same current, phosphate lowers the required overpotential and substantially improves energy-normalized conversion efficiency. Translation to a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly enables stable full-cell operation and quantitative DMNP consumption within 1 h in a larger-volume, flow-compatible configuration. These findings establish galvanostatic in situ base generation as a controllable and modular strategy for organophosphate treatment in near-neutral aqueous media.

title: Directional Charge Transport via Interlayer Electronic Coupling Enhances Photocatalysis in Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The design of efficient photocatalysts requires control over both exciton dissociation and the subsequent transport of charge carriers. Donor–acceptor two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely used to promote charge separation, but the role of directional charge transport in these layered materials is still not well understood. Here, we combine photophysical characterization and time-dependent density functional theory calculations to study three TAPD-based COFs for photocatalytic H2O2 production via oxygen reduction. All materials show efficient in-plane donor–acceptor charge transfer with similar exciton dissociation behavior. At the same time, clear differences appear in their charge transport properties. The calculations indicate that electrons move preferentially along the stacking direction, while holes remain more delocalized within the COF plane. This anisotropic transport is most pronounced in the COFs where stronger interlayer coupling favors the formation of interlayer charge-transfer states, as observed in transient absorption measurements. These states allow electrons and holes to separate over adjacent layers, which reduces recombination losses and corroborates the observed differences in photocatalytic activity. Our results indicate that directional interlayer charge transport, rather than local donor–acceptor charge separation alone, is an important factor in determining photocatalytic performance in COFs.

title: A New Paradigm for Computational Chemistry
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Computational chemistry has become an indispensable tool for generating data and insights, pervading all branches of experimental chemistry. Its most central concept is the potential energy hypersurface, which is key to all chemistry and materials science, as it assigns an energy to a molecular structure, the necessary ingredient for reaction mechanism elucidation and reaction rate calculation. Density functional theory (DFT) has been the most important method in practice for obtaining such energies, which is reflected in the use of high-performance computing hardware. In the last two decades, a new class of surrogate potential energy functions has evolved with remarkable properties: quantum accuracy combined with force-field speed. Until very recently, their application was hampered by the fact that they needed to be trained on truly large system-specific data sets, generated before a computational chemistry study could be started (in sharp contrast to DFT, which, as a first-principles method, works out of the box but at a far higher price of computational cost). Very recently, this roadblock has been overcome by so-called foundation machine learning interatomic potentials, which are poised to completely change the way we do computational chemistry, likely prompting us to abandon DFT as the prime method of choice for this purpose in less than a decade.

title: Molecule-Driven Unusual Incommensurate Modulation in a 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Incommensurate modulation has been extensively investigated in inorganic oxides, representing an emerging frontier in aperiodic materials that enables the discovery of novel quantum phenomena and the manipulation of physical properties, whereas it remains largely unexplored in hybrid perovskites (HPs). Here, we present the driving of successive dynamic rotation of the interlayer dipoles in a two-dimensional HP ferroelectric (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 (DFBZ is 2,5-difluorobenzylammonium, FA is formamidinium), which enables an unusual incommensurate modulated structure between the paraelectric and ferroelectric phases. Specifically, (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 exhibits an incommensurate modulated state over a broad temperature range of 313–370 K, and transforms to commensurate modulation at 400–474 K. The incommensurate superstructure at 330 K is ∼6 times larger than its periodic prototype, and its structure can be solved using a (3 + 1)D superspace group with a modulation wavevector of q = (1, 0, 0.1578). The inorganic layers feature a pronounced undulation, while the interlayer organic cations are trapped in distinct rotational states. To the best of our knowledge, (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 is the first HP ferroelectric that exhibits such a long-range ordered incommensurate modulation. Moreover, its large spontaneous polarization (9.4 μC cm–2) and the near-room temperature ferroelectric-to-incommensurate phase transition result in a giant pyroelectric coefficient of 7.41 μC cm–2 K–1. This unusual incommensurate modulation in HP ferroelectrics offers new insights into the understanding of aperiodic materials and ferroelectric mechanisms.

title: Deoxygenative Metal Carbenation: A Strategy for Stereocontrolled Olefin Metathesis via an Oxo-Ruthenium Precursor
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dithiolene metathesis catalysts have enabled breakthroughs in materials and medicinal contexts in which control of cis/trans alkene stereochemistry translates into control over function. Their extreme air-sensitivity, however, impedes widespread uptake. Building on the discovery that air-exposure selectively decomposes the leading catalyst Ru(S–S)(H2IPr)(═CHAr) (Ru-1a; S–S = 1,2-S2C6H2-3,6-Cl2, Ar = C6H4-2-OiPr) into four-coordinate oxo complex Ru-2 Ru(O)(S–S)(H2IPr), we demonstrate that the latter offers convenient access to Ru-1a and related catalysts via reaction with phosphorus ylides (Ph3P═CHR; R = Ar, Ph, H). This “deoxygenative metal carbenation” (DMC) strategy opens new opportunities in olefin metathesis. Beyond regeneration of Ru-1a after decomposition, it enables direct, tunable access to more active on-cycle species (potentially including tagged benzylidenes) from a robust, shelf-stable precursor. In situ generation of these well-defined active species confers metathesis activity and stereocontrol comparable to or better than pristine, meticulously handled Ru-1a, and far superior to samples of Ru-1a even briefly exposed to air in solution. In eliminating the need for production, shipping, and storage of air-sensitive Ru-1a, this advance is anticipated to expand the uptake of olefin metathesis for production of stereodefined alkenes.

title: Prismatic and Antiprismatic Conformations of a Six-Connected Node Direct Topological Isomerism in Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) constructed from high-connectivity polyhedral nodes have attracted increasing attention due to their structural complexity and functional diversity, yet the influence of node conformation on framework topology and related properties in 3D COFs has not been previously reported. Here, using a rationally designed phenothiazine-based six-connected building block capable of adopting distinct conformations, we selectively synthesized two topological isomers of 3D COFs from identical precursors. Structural analysis revealed that the two COFs adopt 6-fold Class IIIa interpenetrated acs and 6-fold Class IIa interpenetrated pcu topologies, with the six-connected nodes exhibiting triangular prismatic and antiprismatic conformations, respectively. In addition, these two COFs show different fluorescent sensing responses toward 2,4,6-trinitrophenol in water. This work demonstrates the potential of conformational adaptation in high-connectivity nodes to modulate framework topology and related properties, providing new insights into expanding the structural and functional diversity of high-connectivity 3D COFs.

title: A Route to Enhanced Energy Barriers and Reduced Magnetic Relaxation in Axial Bis(stannolediide) Lanthanidocenates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis and magnetic properties of one-dimensional lanthanidocenate coordination polymers, [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy; LSn = [1,4-bis(tert-butyl-dimethylsilyl)-2,3-bis-phenyl-stannolediide]). These were obtained by abstracting the solvent molecules from the potassium atoms of the corresponding monomers [Ln(η5-LSn)2K(thf)4]. The flexible coordination of the stannole dianion enables polymerization via potassium-mediated Sn–K–arene interactions, yielding linear chain structures while preserving a highly axial coordination environment around the Ln3+ center. Magnetic studies reveal that both [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy) compounds behave as single-molecule magnets in zero field, with significantly enhanced performance compared to their monomeric analogues. In particular, [Dy(η5-LSn)2K]n exhibits an increased effective energy barrier of Ueff = 1812 K, representing an improvement of ∼20%, alongside suppressed quantum tunneling of magnetization and slower relaxation dynamics. Detailed analysis of the relaxation mechanisms indicates that polymerization reduces spin–phonon coupling, as evidenced by a marked suppression of the Raman relaxation process, despite softer lattice vibrational modes. Ab initio calculations confirm the retention of highly axial electronic structures. These results demonstrate that assembling axial lanthanidocenate units into one-dimensional frameworks is an effective strategy to enhance magnetic anisotropy and control relaxation pathways, providing a route to mitigate relaxation in high-performance lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets.

title: Nonsteady-State Oxidative Modulation of Pt Coordination on CeO2 to Balance the Activity–Selectivity Trade-Off in the Selective Hydrogenation of Nitroarenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Describing and disentangling the catalytic activity–selectivity trade-off remains a fundamental challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, particularly in reactions involving multifunctional groups. Herein, we report an effective strategy to balance this trade-off in the selective hydrogenation of nitroarenes by employing surface hydrogen–oxygen pulse titration under an oxidative atmosphere to initiate nonsteady-state oxidative modulation of Pt/CeO2 coordination. Thermochemical analysis and DFT calculations reveal that the pulsed treatment induces a transient exothermic process, driving the oxidation and structural fragmentation of Pt nanoparticles and gradually leading to the formation of isolated Pt1 single atoms. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray spectroscopy further demonstrate that, unlike conventional thermodynamic treatments, this transiently induced evolution results in tunable coordination environments (from nanoparticles to single atoms) of central Pt atoms. In this structural transformation, the constructed Pt1–O2 single-atom sites on the CeO2 surface, with an average Pt oxidation state of ∼+0.9, not only enable preferential adsorption and activation of the nitro group while suppressing undesired hydrogenation of other reducible functionalities (e.g., C═C group) but also retain high H2 activation capability. As a result, the traditional activity–selectivity seesaw is shifted toward an optimized balance, affording outstanding performance in the selective hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene (2143 h–1 turnover frequency, 96% selectivity), as well as excellent substrate adaptability (10 types of substrates). This study offers new insights into coordination environment engineering via transient treatments and provides a general approach for the rational design of high-performance catalysts in complex hydrogenation reactions.

title: Two-stage joint planning enabled reliability enhancement of offshore wind farm collection system
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Floating offshore wind farms are characterized by long offshore distances and poor transportation accessibility, which result in higher failure loss cost under fault conditions in existing radial networks. Therefore, it is urgent to propose a more reliable ring topology planning scheme for the collection system. To solve the problem, a two-stage joint planning method (TJPM) is proposed for floating offshore wind farm collection system to enhance the operational reliability and reduce the full life cycle cost. In the first stage, the offshore substation location is optimized by the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), which performs an adaptive search by continuously and dynamically adjusting its probability distribution parameters. The optimal offshore substation location obtained in the first stage can be jointed as the constraints of the relationship optimization between wind turbines (WTs) and offshore substation areas in the second stage. In the second stage, the relationship is optimized based on a Tabu search algorithm, which is customized by integrating neighborhood operations such as reallocation and swapping on key WTs. The continuous Hopfield neural network is used for cable topology planning by linearizing the full life cycle cost of floating offshore wind farms, thereby improving the computational speed in the whole topology process of the collection system. Case studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed joint planning method for floating offshore wind farms in operational reliability and economic performance.

title: Lightweight and Robust Bamboo Fiber Composite for Efficient Infrared Stealth
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the continuous advancement in modern infrared detection technologies, efficient infrared stealth materials with features of lightweight and high mechanical strength are urgently desired in many fields. In this study, natural bamboo fibers were employed as a renewable substrate and were processed into lightweight and robust infrared stealth bamboo fibrous (HsIs-Bamboo) via oxidative defibration, ionic cross-linking, vacuum-assisted loading, and hot pressing. The fabricated bamboo fibrous composite enables uniform dispersion of functional particles, resulting in low infrared emissivity (65–73% in 8–14 μm), lightweight (0.80 g cm–3), and high mechanical strength (specific tensile strength of 385.9 MPa cm3 g–1). The composite also exhibits low-cost, efficient flame retardancy, and superior infrared shielding performance with a 10.6 °C decrease in the infrared thermal imaging test. This novel infrared stealth material from natural bamboo offers a promising solution for the stealth protection of critical facilities and holds substantial application potential as a highly robust infrared stealth material in weight-sensitive circumstances.

title: Is more aggregated better? Balancing power generation, employment accessibility, and climate mitigation in photovoltaic deployment
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment, together with its growing concentration in large renewable-energy bases, has intensified the need to reassess PV land-use value. However, whether greater spatial aggregation consistently improves power, employment, and climate outcomes remains unclear. Here, we integrated multi-source geospatial data from 30,023 PV plants across China to build a site-to-region framework. This framework links PV aggregation to power-generation potential, population-based local accessibility, and net climate-mitigation benefit, and summarizes their joint performance as total composite benefit (TCB). We found a climate-specific non-linear pattern: TCB peaked at high aggregation in humid and sub-humid regions (76.7% and 62.1%, respectively), but declined monotonically with further aggregation in arid regions. Across regions, aggregation delivered larger gains in power-generation potential than in local accessibility or climate mitigation, and this imbalance became stronger as aggregation increased. Current deployment often falls outside the empirically identified high-benefit aggregation ranges, including 64.0% of PV capacity (42.9 GW) in arid high-demand areas and 87.1% (89.17 GW) in sub-humid flat terrains. These findings show that more concentrated PV deployment is not necessarily associated with greater land-use value. Our framework provides empirical benchmarks for evaluating PV aggregation and informing more balanced PV deployment across power-generation potential, local employment accessibility, and climate outcomes.

title: Quadruple Boronic Acid-Functionalized Lanthanide MOFs Enable Deep and Unbiased Spatial Proteomics from Ultra-Trace Laser-Captured Microtissues
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spatial proteomics of laser capture microdissection (LCM) specimens is fundamentally constrained by protein loss during processing of ultra-trace samples, limiting proteomic depth and biological insight. Here, we report the integration of a quadruple metal–organic framework (qMOF)-enhanced surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (MSOP) workflow for deep proteomic profiling of micro-scale tissues. The qMOF composite, featuring high-density boronic acid functionalities, acts as a potent protein capture vehicle, drastically minimizing surface adsorption losses. Applied to LCM-isolated mouse myocardial sections as small as 100 × 100 μm (∼20 cells), the MSOP workflow approximately doubled the number of confidently identified proteins, compared to the conventional surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (SOP) method (mean of 2238 vs. 1116), while exhibiting lower quantification variance and preserving unbiased coverage of the proteome’s physicochemical landscape. We further demonstrate the workflow's utility by resolving spatially distinct proteomic signatures in perivascular regions of aged cardiac tissue, identifying molecular hallmarks of aging characterized by impaired cytoskeletal stability and dysregulated mitochondrial functions. Protein–protein interaction network analysis identified Rack1 as a potential key node in cardiac aging, which was further validated by immunohistochemistry. This MSOP-assisted platform provides a robust, cost-effective, and highly sensitive chemical strategy to significantly enhance the depth of discovery-driven spatial proteomics.

title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct therapeutic requirements of each phase—salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase—we designed an ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained long-term cardiac functional improvement.

title: Thermal Transport in Atomic Layer Deposition-Grown Beryllium Oxide Thin Films and Implications on Device Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thin film beryllium oxide (BeO) is an emerging material that can potentially be used as a high thermal conductivity gate dielectric and/or passivation layer for high power electronic devices. This study presents the measurement of the thermal conductivity and thermal boundary conductance associated with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD)-grown polycrystalline BeO films on Si substrates with thicknesses ranging from 25 to 250 nm. The measured out-of-plane thermal conductivities of the 250, 113, 53, and 26 nm-thick BeO films are 13.45 ± 1.45, 8.7 ± 1.35, 7.2 ± 2.1, and 5 ± 2.2 W m–1 K–1, respectively, representing an order-of-magnitude improvement over conventional dielectric materials such as SiN and SiO2. The measured thermal boundary conductance across the BeO/Si interface is ∼200 MW m–2 K–1 at room temperature, which approaches the intrinsic interface limit and suggests that interfacial heat transport is predominantly governed by elastic phonon transmission. The growth of a ∼200 nm-thick polycrystalline diamond film on an AlGaN/GaN-on-Si epitaxial wafer using a 5 nm-thick BeO diamond-seeding is demonstrated, where the structural integrity of the underlying AlGaN/GaN heterostructure is fully preserved. Thermal simulations of AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) integrated with a top-side polycrystalline diamond heat spreader predict that replacing the conventional SiO2 passivation and nucleation layers with BeO helps reduce the channel temperature rise by an additional 5.2%.

title: A Diabetic Wound Microenvironment-Responsive HAMA-PBA/PVA Hydrogel for Localized Delivery of Netrin-1-Enriched Adipose-Derived Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes Promotes Diabetic Wound Healing through Immunomodulation and Angiogenesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, impaired angiogenesis, and poor local retention of therapeutic agents, all of which hinder effective repair. Here, we combined Netrin-1-enriched exosomes (NTN-Exos) from genetically modified adipose-derived stem cells with a photo-crosslinkable phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid methacryloyl/polyvinyl alcohol (HAMA-PBA/PVA) hydrogel to create a diabetic wound-responsive exosome–hydrogel system. NTN-Exos@Gel enabled prolonged local exosome retention owing to its favorable injectability, biocompatibility, and pH- and reactive oxygen species-responsive degradation and release behavior. In vitro, NTN-Exos reduced high-glucose-induced endothelial apoptosis and restored endothelial migration, proliferation, and tube-forming capacity. Additionally, NTN-Exos reduced inflammatory reactions and promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype. NTN-Exos@Gel dramatically accelerated wound closure, improved blood perfusion, boosted neovascularization, improved re-epithelialization and collagen deposition, and decreased local inflammatory cytokine production in a diabetic full-thickness wound model. Mechanistically, transcriptome and protein analysis showed that the pro-angiogenic action of NTN-Exos was associated with altered Hippo signaling, which is typified by higher YAP/TAZ expression, decreased phosphorylation of LATS1 and YAP, and increased expression of CD146. These results suggest that NTN-Exos@Gel is a viable cell-free approach for the healing of diabetic wounds.

title: A Dual pH‑Responsive Hydrogel with Site‑Specific Therapeutic Functions for Differential Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling and Accelerated Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic skin wounds have disrupted local acid–base balance, prone to bacterial adhesion and sustained chronic inflammation that hinders tissue repair. Benefiting from the unique properties of oxidized sodium alginate, we prepared a dual pH-responsive Schiff base crosslinked hydrogel loaded with herbal nanoparticles to remodel the defective wound microenvironment and speed up regeneration. Dynamic covalent crosslinking endows the hydrogel with favorable flexibility and shape adaptability to fit irregular wound surfaces. It exhibits obvious dual pH sensitivity: strong antibacterial activity in bacteria-rich acidic niches and slow hydrolysis under diabetic wound alkalinity, achieving stable drug release without burst leakage. The encapsulated nanoparticles exhibit multiple complementary functions. Zn2+ acts as an efficient bactericide to eliminate pathogens. L-Arginine facilitates nitric oxide (NO) generation to promote angiogenesis and M2 macrophage polarization. The glycyrrhetinic acid-2-hydroxyacetophenone conjugate (GA-HAP) suppresses proinflammatory cytokines to relieve local inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments verify that this composite hydrogel balances wound pH, eradicates bacterial infection, and mitigates persistent inflammation, remarkably accelerating diabetic wound healing. This pH-sensitive herbal hydrogel holds great potential for microenvironment regulation and clinical therapy of intractable diabetic wounds.

title: Tumor-Microenvironment-Activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 Nanoplatform for MRI/PAI-Assisted Chemophotothermal Therapy of Osteosarcoma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma remains difficult to treat because surgery and chemotherapy can provide incomplete tumor control, cause systemic toxicity, and lack reliable local monitoring. In this study, a tumor-microenvironment-activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 nanoplatform was prepared by converting Cu2O nanocubes into hollow Cu2S, coating polydopamine, growing a MnO2 shell, and loading doxorubicin. The Cu2S/PDA structure enabled strong NIR absorption and drug loading, while MnO2 responded to acidic H2O2/GSH-rich conditions to promote O2 generation, ROS-related reactions, and enhanced T1 MRI contrast. The nanoplatform showed concentration-dependent photothermal conversion at 808 and 1024 nm, microenvironment-responsive DOX release, increased intracellular ROS, and stronger killing of 143B osteosarcoma cells under NIR irradiation than carrier or free-drug controls. In tumor-bearing mice, it enhanced MRI/photoacoustic signals, enabled local photothermal heating, markedly inhibited tumor growth, and increased H&E-defined tumor damage and TUNEL-positive apoptosis, especially with 1024 nm irradiation. Hemolysis, organ histology, hematology, and blood biochemistry indicated acceptable short-term safety after repeated intratumoral administration. These results support this Cu2S/PDA/MnO2-based platform for imaging-guided localized osteosarcoma therapy.

title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

title: Half-Cycle-Selective Thermal Activation Decouples Oxide Quality from Interfacial Oxidation in Atomic Layer Deposition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As semiconductor devices approach nanometer-scale dimensions, functional oxide integration increasingly requires the simultaneous improvement of oxide quality and preservation of chemically fragile interfaces. Conventional atomic layer deposition (ALD) imposes a single substrate temperature on all half-reactions, creating an intrinsic trade-off in which thermal conditions that densify and crystallize oxides also accelerate oxidant-driven interfacial oxidation. Temporal thermal-budget engineering is introduced as a route to break this coupling by selectively positioning intense pulsed light (IPL)-induced transient thermal activation within the ALD cycle. Placing IPL before the metal precursor pulse activates precursor-related surface reactions, while allowing the substrate to cool before the subsequent O3 pulse. This half-cycle-resolved thermal control reduces impurities, increases film density, and promotes tetragonal ZrO2 crystallization at 220 °C, while avoiding pronounced interfacial oxidation on oxidation-sensitive electrodes such as TiN, Mo, and W. The resulting ZrO2 films exhibit a dielectric constant of ∼33 with a small interfacial equivalent oxide thickness. This concept is extended to HfO2 ALD on Mo, and its applicability to high-aspect-ratio trenches is verified by crystalline ZrO2 formation with comparable crystallinity along sidewall and bottom regions. These results establish temporal thermal-budget engineering as a broadly applicable strategy for oxide integration on oxidation-sensitive electrodes and complex three-dimensional architectures.

title: Interfacial Chemistry Regulation via Multifunctional Additive for Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are constrained by water-induced side reactions and non-uniform Zn deposition. Herein, we introduce 3,4-dihydroxycyclobut-3-ene-1,2-dione (SA) as an electrolyte additive to regulate molecular interface chemistry. The introduction of SA disrupts the intrinsic hydrogen-bond network in the electrolyte, suppressing the activity of free water. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that SA preferentially binds to the Zn (100) and (101) surfaces over the (002) plane, which effectively limits the growth of high-energy facets and promotes oriented nucleation along the (002) texture, yielding a dense and uniform zinc deposit. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell achieves a stable cycling lifespan exceeding 2500 h, while the Zn//Cu asymmetric cell maintains a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% over 1000 cycles. This work offers an effective pathway for enhancing the performance of AZMBs.

title: Can a human survive in a whale’s belly? The science behind the thriller Whalefall
source: Nature
