title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals.

title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS3, in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX2, previously reported as having inverted S1-T1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX2 show anti-Kasha S0←S2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S0→S1, linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S0→S2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S0←S1 emission, whereas exciting S0→S1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S2 and S1 is very weak, S2-TN intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S1↔T1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T1→S1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale.

title: Cavity-Selective Host–Guest Assembly for Modular Buried-Interface Engineering in Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we use cavity-selective host–guest recognition to construct a modular, recognition-directed interface. The cavity of dipolar 4-tert-butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene (tBSCA) selectively accommodates the terminal phenyl group of substrate-anchored Ph-4PACz. Comparisons with a structurally related calixarene analogue and competing inclusion orientations identify a thermodynamically preferred Ph-4PACz-tBSCA configuration, distinguishing cavity-selective association from nonspecific interactions. This preferred configuration underpins a preferentially organized dipolar interface that retains Ph-4PACz-mediated anchoring and charge transport while enabling tBSCA to regulate interfacial electrostatics, reduce interfacial defect sites, and suppress defect-assisted halide migration and interfacial accumulation. The resulting devices achieve a PCE of 27.36% (certified at 26.74%), and a 110 cm2 module delivers a certified efficiency of 22.61%. These results demonstrate configuration-selective molecular recognition as a strategy for the modular organization of complementary functions at buried perovskite interfaces.

title: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

title: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

title: First-principles channel model and capacity-achieving transmission scheme in thermal noise backscatter links
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and radio frequency identification tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range—over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

title: CX3CL1 (fractalkine)–CX3CR1 interface drives CD8⁺ T cell–induced neurodegeneration in human brain organoids
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Immune–neuron interactions play a critical role in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but how CD8⁺ T cells contribute to brain pathology remains poorly understood. Amyloid-β (Aβ), a hallmark of AD, is known to trigger neuronal stress and inflammation. Here, we established a human cortical organoid (hCO) model to investigate CD8⁺ T cell responses to Aβ-induced neurodegenerative stress. Aβ exposure increased neuronal expression of CX3CL1 (fractalkine), which engages its receptor CX3CR1 on CD8⁺ T cells. Transwell migration assays showed enhanced recruitment of CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells toward Aβ-treated hCOs. In parallel, Aβ upregulated IL-15 expression, a cytokine that supports CD8⁺ T cell activation. The infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells led to neuronal injury, marked by MAP2 loss and cleaved Caspase-3 activation, accompanied by an increase in gene signatures for cell death and inflammation. Exposure to the conditioned medium of activated CX3CR1
                    high
                    CD8⁺ T cell recapitulated this damage, and the neutralization of CD8
                    +
                    T cell cytokines and cytotoxic molecules rescued the phenotype. These findings identify the CX3CL1–CX3CR1 axis and CD8⁺ T cell effector programs as drivers of neurotoxicity and establish brain organoids as a platform to study immune-driven neurodegeneration.

title: Transient ATM inhibition enhances knock-in efficiency in hematopoietic stem cells by attenuating the DNA damage response
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Precise genome editing in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) holds great potential for treating inherited blood disorders; however, low knock-in (KI) efficiency and loss of functional HSCs after genome editing remain major obstacles. Here, we demonstrate that transient inhibition of Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated (ATM) kinase markedly enhanced KI efficiency in mouse HSCs genome-edited with Cas9/ribonucleoprotein (RNP) and AAV donor DNA. Phosphoproteomic and capillary western blot analyses revealed that ATM inhibition suppressed aberrant Cas9-AAV-induced ATM activation and the subsequent DNA damage response, reduced p53-dependent apoptosis, and enhanced survival of KI HSCs. In serial transplantation assays, ATM inhibition preserved long-term engrafting KI HSCs, increasing their frequency from ~0.3 to 40% in secondary recipients, an over 100-fold improvement. Furthermore, in an X-linked severe combined immunodeficient mouse model, ATM inhibition increased KI efficiency and restored T- and B cell differentiation. Comprehensive safety analyses, including long-read nanopore sequencing, amplicon deep sequencing, whole genome sequencing and clonal tracking, did not detect increased genomic alterations, chromosomal abnormalities, or clonal expansion following transient ATM inhibition. Taken together, these findings establish transient ATM inhibition as an effective strategy to enhance KI-mediated genome editing while maintaining the long-term repopulating capacity of HSCs.

title: Connexins are essential for the contribution of latent progenitors to healing after spinal cord injury
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Gap junctions are important regulators of the biology of neural stem cells. Both in vertebrates with regenerative abilities and neonatal rodents, ependymal cells communicate via connexin (Cx) 43 and Cx26. Gap junction coupling and Cx26 are down-regulated as the ependyma becomes quiescent in adulthood, but injury overrules this developmental down-regulation suggesting a role for Cx signaling in the reactivation of ependymal cells. However, direct evidence of the involvement of these Cxs in the reactivation of the ependymal stem cell niche is lacking. Here, we aim to explore the role of Cx26 and Cx43 in the response of ependymal cells to injury by means of specific genetic deletion. We find that Cx26 is critical for the proliferative response of ependymal cells to injury. The reduced response of ependymal cells by Cx26 deletion increased the extension of the lesion because of impaired healing resulting from a weak contribution of the ependymal stem cell niche. On the other hand, Cx43—via gap junction coupling and hemichannels—plays a key role in the communication of Ca
                    2+
                    signals between ependymal cells induced by activation of P2X7 receptors. Our data show that Cxs are relevant targets to manipulate the ependymal stem cell niche to achieve better healing after spinal cord injury.

title: Lhx9 specifically modulates phalanx number, whereas Lhx2 constrains digit length in tetrapods
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Most nonmammalian tetrapods exhibit more than three phalanges in their posterior digits (III–V), whereas mammals are restricted to no more than three. So far, the molecular mechanism underlying this evolutionary reduction and the functions of
                    Lhx2
                    and
                    Lhx9
                    in digit development remain unclear. Here we show divergent evolution of
                    Lhx2
                    and
                    Lhx9
                    expression patterns in embryonic limbs across tetrapods. We further demonstrate that although ectopic overexpression of each gene in chick embryos delayed limb skeletal development, only
                    Lhx9
                    reduced the phalanx number in the posterior digits. Transcriptomic analysis showed that
                    Lhx2
                    regulates pathways for chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation, and
                    Lhx9
                    preferentially influences skeletal segmentation via the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) pathway. The unique function and differential expression of
                    Lhx9
                    in the limb buds between mammals and nonmammalian tetrapods suggest it may have acquired a role in suppressing phalanx number, driving the evolutionary reduction of phalanx number in mammals.

title: Mediator-associated proteins and the small RNA–guided Polycomb repressive complex enhance cryptic transcription for transposon exclusion
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Suppression of transposable elements (TEs) is critical for maintaining genome integrity. The evolutionary arms race between TEs and their eukaryotic host organisms has driven the development of small RNA–dependent mechanisms that specifically suppress TEs while leaving non-TE regions unperturbed. In the binucleated ciliate
                    Tetrahymena
                    , small RNAs (sRNAs) are generated from both TE and non-TE regions of the germline genome, whereas noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) from the TE-free somatic genome target and eliminate non-TE sRNAs, thereby selectively preserving TE-specific sRNAs for guiding TE recognition. Since sRNAs are produced from both strands, the counteracting ncRNAs must also occur bidirectionally. However, the mechanism by which the somatic genome generates ncRNAs from both strands remains unresolved. Here, we show that these ncRNAs arise from widespread cryptic transcription initiated outside canonical promoters and dependent on the developmentally specific Mediator complex–associated proteins Dima1 and Emit2. We further demonstrate that sRNA-guided recruitment of the
                    Tetrahymena
                    Polycomb repressive complex 2 and Dima1 occupancy are mutually reinforcing, promoting local accumulation of RNA polymerase II, which may facilitate cryptic transcription from these loci in a histone methyltransferase-independent manner. Disruption of Dima1 abolishes cryptic transcription, leads to aberrant accumulation of non-TE sRNAs, and results in erroneous genome elimination and cell death. These findings reveal a regulatory circuit involving sRNAs, Polycomb, and the Mediator-associated protein Dima1 that promotes cryptic transcription, thereby ensuring accurate TE exclusion and genome integrity.

title: Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft observations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is linked to Mars’ extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar wind, this finding bears on solar–wind interactions at comets and other small bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind–planet coupling at unmagnetized worlds.

title: Screw dislocation–mediated galaxy-mimicking superspiral assembly with amplified bio-piezoelectricity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: From the galaxies to the petals, spiral architectures are ubiquitous to confer hierarchical organizations, supporting asymmetric galactic evolutions and biological activities. Herein, inspired from nature, we report the superspiral architectures self-assembled by a minimalist amino acid. These superspirals, with spirality and geometry programmably tuned by enantiomeric excess and organization parameters, are determined to arise from the screw dislocation induced hierarchical crystallization. Notably, the spiral organization can integrate and amplify electrical polarization, yielding 17-fold enhancement in piezoelectric response contrast to random aggregates. This allows engineering of piezoelectric bioelectronics, resulting in high gain direction-selective motion sensing. Our work establishes an alternative paradigm for developing bioinspired hierarchical architectures of oriented and amplified properties, offering a self-assembling route to explore programmably modulated functional architectures for bioelectronic engineering.

title: The susceptibility to weight gain in male C57BL/6 mice fed high-fat diet is due to a small set of genes predominantly not expressed in the brain
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Obesity results from a gene by environment interaction. Understanding the impacts of environmental factors like diet on body weight/fatness has been greatly facilitated by rodent models. We previously identified the responses of males of five mouse strains fed 30 different diets. Two of these strains showed much greater weight gain and two were resistant. Sixty-six marker SNPs in 57 genes were identified, which have a genetic motif across the four strains reflecting their protection or susceptibility to high-fat diet (HFD). We used two of these strains: C57BL/6 and BALB/c, in a classic approach of cross-breeding the strains, to generate a F1 generation, and then cross-breeding their offspring to generate an F2 population. The F2 males were fed HFD and phenotyped for body weight, fat mass, and energy intake and genotyped for the 66 SNPs. Body mass gain on HFD was influenced by 17 SNPs in 11 genes explaining 87% of the individual variation in weight gain. We then measured gene expression of these 11 genes in 16 tissues of male and female C57BL/6 and Balb/c mice when fed high- or low-fat diets, and in 6 tissues of mice exposed to different levels of calorie restriction, to map their expression profiles. The genes were widely expressed in a diversity of tissues including several not normally suspected to be important for fat storage regulation (e.g., testis, lungs, and spleen) with only four expressed predominantly in the hypothalamus. Body fat regulation is probably more complex than current models focused on the brain–adipose axis suppose.

title: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

title: Evolution of the arbuscular mycorrhizal regulatory network through differential GRAS gene retention and protein interaction in land plants
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Plants rely on an ancient genetic “toolkit” to establish arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis (AMS) with fungal partners. However, the symbiotic outcomes vary among AMS hosts, indicating divergence in downstream transcriptional reprogramming after the perception of symbiotic signals. To uncover the cross-species variation of the AMS regulatory network, we traced the evolutionary trajectory of the GRAS gene family, which encodes the major group of transcription factors in AMS regulation. Phylogenetic analysis of the GRAS family across land plants placed known symbiotic GRAS members within 12 anciently diverged lineages, with multiple lineages showing pronounced gene loss in nonmycorrhizal plants. This pattern pointed to three additional GRAS lineages as candidates for AMS regulation. Given that tomato harbors single-copy, AMS-induced genes in these lineages, we selected it for functional validation. CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis, combined with detailed phenotyping of fungal colonization and arbuscule morphology, and transcriptome profiling of mutant roots, confirmed that all three tomato genes are individually required for AMS development, designated Symbiosis-Required GRAS (SRG) 1 to 3. Large-scale phylogenomic analysis and protein interaction assays (by yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation) further showed that both the repertoire and interaction networks of symbiotic GRAS members vary among AMS hosts. In summary, together with 12 previously characterized lineages, the three SRGs identified in this study bring the total number of GRAS lineages with known symbiotic members across land plants to fifteen. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the symbiotic GRAS network has been dynamically reshaped by gene loss and rewiring of protein interactions during land plant evolution.

title: Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut–lung axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Respiratory infections remain a major global health challenge, further compounded by antibiotic resistance. Among these, mycoplasmal pneumonia represents a particularly prevalent and refractory form. Here, using targeted enzymatic fragmentation combined with multidimensional NMR analysis, we resolved the structure of a homogeneous
                    Ganoderma lucidum
                    polysaccharide, GLFP2, and identified β-(1→6)-linked galactosyl motifs as key structural features. Despite minimal systemic absorption, oral GLFP2 alleviated mycoplasmal pneumonia in mice. Instead, GLFP2 reshaped the gut microbiota and functionally reprogrammed gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs), whose transplantation alone was sufficient to confer pulmonary protection. Orally administered GMEVs remained bioactive, showed systemic exposure, associated with the lung, and were preferentially taken up by alveolar macrophages. These vesicles activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, suppressed the S100A8/A9 inflammatory axis, and limited neutrophil-driven immunopathology. Collectively, these findings identify microbiota-derived vesicles as effectors of gut–lung communication and use a defined polysaccharide to uncover a remote protective mechanism against pneumonia.

title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

title: Magnetically guided programmable thermomechanical protection enabled by biomimetic asymmetric design
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Precision instruments operating in harsh environments require protective materials that can dissipate impact energy while resisting heat. However, actively tunable thermomechanical protection under coupled multiphysics conditions remains challenging. Inspired by shellfish and echinoderms, here we show that an asymmetrically engineered shear-stiffening gel (SSG) yields a Janus magnetorheological elastomer whose two faces mimic the brick-and-mortar architecture of shellfish and the impact-hardening behavior of echinoderms, respectively. Unlike single-modification anti-creep strategies of SSG that degrade shear-stiffening or severely increase initial modulus, our design achieves a 40-fold mechanical tunability, with the storage modulus ranging from 11.29 to 450.28 kPa, arising from the synergistic enhancement of strain-rate-dependent stiffening and magnetic interactions. The integration of magnetic and optical functions enables semiactive noncontact 2D-to-3D protection, achieving an 85% reduction in impact force and a 40 °C temperature difference via bidirectional photothermal regulation, demonstrating competitive thermomechanical protection performance. Furthermore, this strategy establishes a magnetically guided programmable pathway for thermomechanical protection and provides a generalizable blueprint for multifunctional intelligent materials, advancing protective technologies for outdoor equipment operating in extreme environments involving coupled physical fields.

title: Programmable chemoenzymatic synthesis of a keratan sulfate N-glycan library for glycocode decoding
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Keratan sulfate (KS) is a unique and widely distributed glycosaminoglycans family implicated in diverse biological processes. KS features branched glycan architectures with diverse sialylation and sulfation patterns, encoding a vastly expanded chemical and biological space. The limited accessibility of well-defined structures has hindered precise investigations into the KS biological functions. Here we report a programmable chemoenzymatic platform for assembling a 106-membered library of KS
                    N
                    -glycans and their nonsulfated counterparts, featuring length-variable oligo-
                    N
                    -acetyllactosamine (LacNAc) extensions and encompassing diverse sulfation and sialylation patterns. The synthetic strategy integrates length-controlled iterative glycosylation to assemble versatile precursors, orthogonal deprotection for site-specific sulfation, and modular enzyme-driven diversification. Glycan microarray analysis of this comprehensive library reveals that glycan–protein recognition is governed by the interplay of sulfation and sialylation patterns, oligo-LacNAc chain length, and terminal epitope presentation, providing insight into the functional versatility of KS glycans.

title: Conformational flexibility of the nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D involved in coenzyme F430 biosynthesis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D catalyzes the six-electron reduction of the tetrapyrrole macrocycle of Ni
                    2+
                    -sirohydrochlorin
                    a,c
                    -diamide during the biosynthesis of coenzyme F
                    430
                    , an essential cofactor for biological methane formation and consumption. The individual dimeric protein components, CfbC
                    2
                    and CfbD
                    2
                    , form a complex to allow for electron transfer from the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbC
                    2
                    to the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbD
                    2
                    and onto the substrate. The overall process is ATP-dependent. Although CfbC/D belongs to the family of nitrogenase-like enzymes, there are several intriguing differences between CfbC/D, other nitrogenase-like enzymes and nitrogenase itself. In contrast to the other enzymes, CfbC/D exhibits a simpler molecular architecture, forming a heterotetrameric CfbC
                    2
                    D
                    2
                    assembly. Furthermore, the interaction of the CfbC and CfbD components does not depend on the presence of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the CfbC/D complex prepared in the absence and presence of substrates. These structures not only shed light on the molecular architecture of the CfbC/D complex but also reveal a high degree of structural flexibility within the CfbD
                    2
                    component, which undergoes a large conformational change in the presence of an ATP analog and the tetrapyrrole substrate. The interplay of CfbD with its reductase CfbC also strongly suggests an evolutionary pathway toward the modern nitrogenase from methanogenic archaea.

title: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: One of the key events in the HIV-1 life cycle is reverse transcription (RT), during which single-stranded viral RNA (ssRNA) is converted into double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). This process occurs inside the mature HIV-1 capsid and, once it reaches a critical threshold, drives capsid rupture. This uncoating is essential for infection because it releases viral genetic material into the host cell nucleus. Despite its importance, many mechanistic details of this process remain to be fully understood. To address this gap, we develop a multiscale computational method for simulating RT inside the capsid, termed Coarse-Grained Kinetic Monte Carlo (CG-KMC). CG-KMC stochastically adds deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs) to the coarse-grained RNA model, enabling stepwise growth of DNA inside the HIV-1 capsid. We implement this method within an integrative coarse-grained framework that combines a “bottom-up” capsid model with a “top-down” representation of the viral RNA/DNA genome. Our simulations phenomenologically capture and predict diverse capsid rupture pathways during RT. The resulting ruptured structures closely match previously identified cryo-ET images. We further perform an extensive analysis of the rupture process, examining its mechanistic and kinetic aspects as well as the role of capsid–DNA interactions. Our findings illuminate how different capsid–DNA conditions give rise to distinct rupture pathways, which differ from ruptures due to simple outward pressure expansion models from within the capsid.

title: Methanogenic archaea Methanobrevibacter smithii and Methanosphaera stadtmanae promote mucosal homeostasis and protect from colitis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The intestinal microbiota is a critical determinant of mucosal homeostasis, yet the functional contributions of Archaea—which constitute up to 10% of the anaerobic community—remain largely undefined. Here, we provide evidence that the human methanogens
                    Methanobrevibacter smithii
                    (MSm) and
                    Methanosphaera stadtmanae
                    (MSt) promote colonic health. Transcriptomic analysis of germ-free mice reveals that MSm and MSt induce distinct colonic programs important for epithelial integrity. Using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-treated specific-pathogen-free mouse models, we show that MSm and MSt reinforce the epithelial barrier, characterized by increased goblet cell expansion, mucus thickening, and enhanced epithelial regeneration. Furthermore, methanogens expand Foxp3
                    +
                    regulatory T cell (T
                    reg
                    ) populations without inducing pro-inflammatory T
                    H
                    17 responses. Notably, MSm and MSt protect against dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis. While MSt-mediated protection requires adaptive immunity, MSm retains partial efficacy in lymphocyte-deficient mice, revealing nonredundant protective mechanisms. These findings indicate that methanogenic archaea promote mucosal integrity during host association and suggest that methanogens may hold therapeutic potential for inflammatory bowel disease, though translation to human disease remains to be established.

title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains—carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)—as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of specific high-risk EBV lineages and their synergistic interaction with host immune susceptibility. This provides a definitive genetic framework for precision population screening and early diagnosis of NPC in the endemic regions.

title: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Climate change and technology diffusion will jointly drive future growth in building electricity demand. How this nonadditive response evolves over time with the pace of climate change and technology diffusion has not previously been examined, despite its importance for maintaining reliable power systems. We estimate electricity demand from residential and commercial buildings under climate change and/or technology diffusion across 183 counties in the United States through 2060. Our framework drives 209,352 machine learning models of building electricity demand with 100 spatiotemporally downscaled climate realizations across four climate models and three emissions scenarios, and 18 technology diffusion pathways of air source heat pumps and insulation. We find that the combined response of peak demand to climate change and technology diffusion diverges substantially from the sum of their individual responses, with distinct patterns across hot and cold grid regions. In cold regions, climate change and technology diffusion drive roughly up to 10 times larger peak demand growth than climate change alone by 2060. Conversely, in hot regions, technology diffusion counteracts climate-change-driven peak demand growth. Across regions, climate-change-induced warming reduces or eliminates a shift toward winter peaking driven by technology diffusion. Via uncertainty partitioning, we find climate-related uncertainty dominates near-term peak demand uncertainty, while technology-diffusion-related uncertainty increases to 10 to 80% of uncertainty by 2060. Internal variability accounts for a much larger share of climate-related uncertainty in peak demand than in temperature itself. Our results demonstrate that capturing nonadditive responses between climate change and technology diffusion is important for planning reliable power systems.

title: PSF3 recruits Polθ to stalled replication forks to promote DNA repair
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: DNA polymerase theta (Polθ) plays a pivotal role in the maintenance of stalled replication forks. However, little is known about how Polθ is recruited to the stalled forks. Here we show that PSF3, a member of GINS replicative complex, recruits Polθ to the stalled replication forks. Polθ, which is recruited by interacting with the C-terminal portion of PSF3, restarts the forks, exerts DNA double-strand break end-joining to repair the breaks resulting from collapsed forks in BRCA1/2-deficient and proficient tumor cells, and also fills single-stranded gaps on the replication fork lagging strand in BRCA1/2-deficient tumor cells. Thus, PSF3–Polθ interaction promotes the proliferation of homologous recombination-deficient and proficient tumor cells. Overall, this study highlights an important mechanism of Polθ recruitment to the stalled replication forks to maintain Polθ-dependent fork protection in tumor cells.

title: A tunable immune-evasion function of Zika virus NS5 governs viral fitness and pathogenesis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Type I interferon (IFN) signaling is a central antiviral defense, with STAT2 driving the expression of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) to restrict viral infection. Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus evade this pathway through nonstructural protein 5 (NS5)-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of STAT2, yet the contribution of this immune-evasion strategy to viral fitness and pathogenesis remains incompletely defined. Here, using a multistep mutational scanning strategy that jointly assessed STAT2 degradation and viral RNA replication, we identified a single NS5 residue, L162, as uniquely permissive to substitution that abolishes STAT2 degradation without compromising intrinsic replication functions. Substitution of L162 with alanine or glycine (L162A or L162G) selectively disrupted NS5 recruitment of the ZSWIM8-CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby preserving STAT2 stability and restoring IFN signaling. Recombinant ZIKV carrying these mutations exhibited reduced replication and enhanced ISG induction in human cells, defects fully rescued by STAT2 knockout. In A129 mice (type I IFN receptor deficient), mutant and WT viruses replicated comparably, but in human STAT2 knock-in mice, ZIKV-NS5
                    L162G
                    exhibited markedly reduced viral loads and disease. In pregnant human STAT2 knock-in mice, the mutant also reduced placental and fetal viral burdens and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Notably, infection with ZIKV-NS5
                    L162G
                    elicited robust neutralizing antibody and T cell responses that conferred protection against WT challenge. Together, these findings establish NS5-mediated STAT2 degradation as a central determinant of ZIKV immune-evasion, viral fitness, and pathogenesis and highlight disruption of NS5–STAT2 antagonism as a promising strategy for antiviral intervention and rational attenuation.

title: Structure of bovine viral diarrhea virus E2 glycoprotein in complex with CD46 reveals the molecular basis of virus–receptor recognition
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) is a major contagious pathogen of ruminants and imposes substantial economic burdens on the global livestock industry. The viral envelope glycoprotein E2 mediates host cell attachment by recognizing the CD46 receptor; however, the molecular basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structure of BVDV-1 E2 in complex with bovine CD46 at 3.1-Å resolution. The structure reveals that the SCR1-2 domains of CD46 engage the DII-DIV domains of E2 in a roughly antiparallel orientation. Atomic interactions at the E2/CD46 interface are dominated by van der Waals contacts, accompanied by only a limited number of hydrogen bonds, which explains the observed low-affinity binding between the two molecules. Structural analysis and mutagenesis studies identify key receptor features that govern host susceptibility to the virus and propose an interesting bipartite model: The D′/D interloop within SCR1 of CD46 likely serves as the “molecular determinant,” and key interface residues within SCR2 function as the “affinity regulator.” We further engineered CD46 decoy proteins exhibiting over 1,800-fold higher apparent binding to E2 than the wild-type receptor and demonstrated their potent virus-neutralizing activity. Collectively, these findings elucidate the molecular basis of CD46 recognition by BVDV, provide a structural framework for understanding the viral host range, and establish a receptor-based strategy for potential antiviral intervention.

title: Ecological, physiological, and evolutionary drivers of stoichiometry in insects
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The elemental composition of organisms links physiology to biogeochemical cycles, yet the relative contributions of evolutionary divergence, ecology, and allometry to stoichiometric variation remain incompletely resolved. Here, we integrate a global insect stoichiometric database spanning 223 species with a comprehensive phylogenetic backbone to evaluate the relative importance of hypothesized ecophysiological drivers of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry within a multivariate framework. We found a strong phylogenetic signal in stoichiometric ratios and in P and N content, with evolutionary divergence (phylogenetic structure) accounting for approximately half of the explained variation in P-based ratios, exceeding the contribution of any individual ecological predictor. Phylogenetically corrected models recover trophic enrichment across successive trophic levels, consistent with previously documented patterns, and positive scaling between body mass and both C:P and N:P, in line with the general predictions of the Growth Rate Hypothesis. Temperature was the strongest ecological predictor of insect stoichiometry, with positive effects on C:P and N:P ratios and a negative effect on C:N, highlighting the thermal underpinnings of previously observed geographic patterns. Finally, our models recover higher P and lower C in terrestrial insects relative to their aquatic counterparts, contrary to classic expectations that invoke differences in structural constraints and autotrophic composition across habitats. Together, our work shows that variation in insect stoichiometry emerges from the interacting influences of evolutionary divergence and ecological and physiological variation, which can be disentangled through appropriately scaled, phylogenetically informed analyses.

title: Molecular basis for discrimination of cGAMP linkage isomers by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Riboswitches are noncoding RNA regulatory motifs predominantly found in bacteria. Signaling molecules such as c-di-GMP, c-di-AMP, and 3′,3′-cGAMP have been reported to be recognized by riboswitches. In contrast, 2′,3′-cGAMP functions as a second messenger in mammalian cells, yet its interaction with RNA molecules remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structures of a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant, c-di-GMP-II-Bh, bound to 2′,3′-cGAMP and 3′,3′-cGAMP. Both complexes adopt a similar overall RNA scaffold with an identical binding pocket composition. However, the ligand bases adopt inverted orientations in the binding pocket, resulting in distinct interaction patterns with residues A64 and G68 and differences in base-pair stacking against the phosphodiester backbone. Structural comparison together with ligand-binding assays of structure-guided mutants using isothermal titration calorimetry reveals the molecular principles by which an RNA riboswitch discriminates among cyclic dinucleotide linkage isomers, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of RNA binding pockets to subtle ligand structural variations and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding ligand specificity in RNA–small molecule recognition.

title: Multiple sources contribute to predictive tactile attenuation in the mouse whisker system
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The brain predicts action outcomes using interacting neuronal systems that integrate sensory feedback, movement, and rewards. In the mouse whisker system, we investigated whether two presumed predictive mechanisms jointly attenuate ascending tactile signals during movement. To this end, we employed an open-loop whisker-reach task that monitored facial nucleus motor activity and presented experimental tactile consequences while measuring tactile attenuation in the barrel cortex. Experimentally manipulating sensory consequences revealed two distinct systems. Sensory gating, a previously documented but functionally unclear mechanism of tactile attenuation, appeared graded but persisted during and after movement. In contrast, a second system was found to be temporally precise, generate suppression when stimuli are omitted, and capable of being learned within hundreds of trials. We label it state estimation as its characteristics—active suppression of expected tactile input—aligns well with the classical reafference principle, previously overlooked in the whisker system.

title: Heterogeneous amyloid β dimerization revealed by single-molecule FRET and MD simulation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The correlation between specific amyloid fibril polymorphs and diseases suggests that characterization of heterogeneity in the aggregation process is key to understanding disease mechanisms. In this work, we use single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to quantitatively characterize dimerization of amyloid β (Aβ), the first step of the aggregation process. We find that dimerization is extremely rare, with a high dissociation constant of >16 mM, yet there are multiple dimer states with distinct FRET efficiencies and stabilities, many of which survive for milliseconds to seconds. The dimer population increases with the increasing ionic strength and decreasing pH, indicating the importance of nonspecific electrostatic interactions in dimer formation. MD simulations with enhanced sampling demonstrate the formation of diverse bound states having a range of FRET efficiencies and flexible N termini, compatible with the experimental observations. There are conformational clusters represented by the formation of three mixed parallel/antiparallel β strands forming Greek key-like motifs and the formation of antiparallel β strands, which may be representative of dimers with longer and shorter lifetimes, respectively, observed in the FRET experiment. This structural and kinetic heterogeneity, resulting from transient interactions, reflects the rugged energy landscape of amyloid formation and may be related to the great diversity of fibrils ultimately formed in the aggregation process.

title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

title: Interface engineering of Pt-based catalysts toward enhanced methanol oxidation in direct methanol fuel cells
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are promising power sources, but their practical performance remains limited by sluggish methanol oxidation, CO poisoning, Pt-site degradation, and low Pt utilization. This review critically examines Pt-centered interface engineering for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) in DMFC anodes. First, MOR pathways, performance descriptors, in situ and operando methods, and the factors governing the transfer of half-cell activity to DMFC output are assessed. Representative catalysts are then compared according to the dominant kinetic or degradation limitation addressed by their local interfaces, covering adsorption regulation, pathway control, oxygen-species cooperation, Pt-site retention or regeneration, and cooperative low-Pt utilization. The analysis assigns the dominant function of multifunctional interfaces, evaluates that function using process-specific evidence, and determines whether it survives working-state evolution and membrane electrode assembly integration. Cross-case comparison shows that material class does not uniquely define function and that similar activity, CO tolerance, or durability may arise from different mechanisms. It further distinguishes suppression of adsorbed CO (CO ads) formation from oxidation of pre-adsorbed CO ads , nominal oxophilicity from verified water activation, and structural retention from functional retention and controlled regeneration. Finally, problem-matched design rules are proposed for efficient, low-Pt, and durable DMFC anodes.

title: From gas generation to intelligent management: a gas-signal-driven framework for thermal runaway early warning in lithium-ion batteries
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries poses a critical challenge to the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems. Conventional battery management systems (BMSs), which primarily rely on voltage and temperature signals, frequently exhibit delayed response and limited capability for early-stage fault detection. Gas signals, generated at the early stages of TR, provide rich physicochemical information on internal reactions and offer unique potential for timely warning and fault diagnosis. This review presents a gas-signal-driven early warning framework that systematically integrates mechanism understanding, signal sensing, and intelligent decision-making. The framework is designed to upgrade current BMS architectures without major hardware redesign. Specifically, this review (i) deconstructs multi-stage gas generation mechanisms, characteristic gas fingerprints across different battery chemistries, and their spatiotemporal evolution; (ii) critically evaluates state-of-the-art gas sensing technologies and their applicability to practical battery systems; and (iii) synthesizes intelligent early warning architectures, with an emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and AI-based methods to enhance detection reliability, extend warning lead time, and enable predictive safety interventions. In addition, key engineering challenges-including trace gas detection under realistic conditions, environmental interference, long-term sensor stability, and constraints for edge deployment-are systematically discussed. Future directions toward cloud-edge collaboration are also outlined. Beyond early warning, this infrastructure also holds promise for full-lifecycle management, including state estimation and maintenance scheduling.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Dynamics-aware scheduling of renewable electrolyzer plants: A physics-informed reinforcement learning approach
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Producing hydrogen via renewable electrolyzer plants (REPs) is crucial for reducing carbon emissions in industrial sectors. Meanwhile, with renewable energy generation and electrolyzer units integrated at a common grid connection, these plants provide high-quality resources for regulating power grid operations. Nonetheless, fully utilizing this potential relies on the profitable operation of REPs across joint energy and frequency containment reserve markets in conjunction with the application of data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) scheduling approaches to counteract the stochasticity in renewable generation and the volatility of markets. However, current scheduling frameworks often neglect detailed internal thermal-electrical dynamics and discrete operational states, which result in sub-optimal or physically infeasible policies. The present work addresses this issue by proposing a comprehensive imitation-enhanced RL (IE-RL) scheduling framework. First, the framework incorporates a physics-informed neural network surrogate model to capture transient electrolyzer dynamics accurately. Then, the operational environment is decoupled into continuous subspaces based on whether the electrolyzer unit is in the on state or in the standby state, and dedicated expert policies are pre-trained for each operational environment. Finally, the IE-RL agent is trained to imitate the expert policy matching the current active operational state accurately. The results of numerical computations demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances joint-market profitability while maintaining high physical fidelity with a significantly accelerated training process.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Loss factor-based tandem power generation unit for ionic osmotic energy conversion
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Ionic osmotic energy conversion harnesses salinity-gradient energy through selective ion transport in charged nanochannels. While existing studies primarily focus on high-performance single-unit materials, large-scale applications require integration of multiple units to enhance power output. However, strong nonlinear coupling among ion transport, charge accumulation, and interfacial processes prevents simple linear scaling of individual unit performance, with key parameters and their coupling mechanisms at the system level remaining poorly understood. In this study, a loss factor ( Lf ) is proposed to quantify power loss in tandem power generation units (T–PGU). Based on an equivalent circuit model, a quantitative relationship between Lf and the electrical signal ratios of individual units in T–PGU is established. System parameters are further classified into shared operating and channel-specific categories for investigating power output and energy loss under varying conditions through experiments and simulations. Results reveal a trade-off between maximum output power ( P max ) and Lf with concentration variations. Increasing temperature enhances P max with minimal impact on Lf , while KCl electrolytes significantly improve performance, reducing Lf to 4 × 10 −4 compared to NaCl and LiCl. Additionally, tuning nanochannels with lower current enables simultaneous improvement in power output and reduction in Lf . Based on these findings, an optimization strategy involving temperature elevation, electrolyte substitution, and surface charge matching with pH regulation is proposed and validated, achieving 283% increase in P max and 92.5% reduction in Lf . This work provides a theoretical and experimental foundation for system-level optimization and scalable design of ionic osmotic power generation.

title: Degradation-aware optimization of SOFC operating strategies under off-design balance-of-plant dynamics
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems face significant performance and cost challenges due to stack degradation and the resulting off-design operation of balance-of-plant (BoP) components. This study presents an optimization framework for SOFC operation that explicitly accounts for stack degradation and off-design BoP dynamics. A 10-cell hydrogen-fueled SOFC stack was fabricated and tested under varied flow and humidity conditions to obtain polarization data, which were used to calibrate the system model with an R 2 of 94.7–99.2%. The calibrated model, coupled with surrogate-based optimization, enables time-segmented scheduling of current density and fuel utilization with periodic setpoint updates over a 20-year techno-economic assessment based on levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), electrical efficiency, and lifetime electricity output. The results show that, under the assumptions of the representative case study, the optimized schedules can reduce LCOE by up to 16%, increase lifetime electrical efficiency by more than 10 percentage points, and increase cumulative electricity output by nearly 20%. In addition, the sensitivity of the optimal schedules to the adjustment interval reveals practical trade-offs between economic performance and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to identify improved long-term SOFC operating strategies under degradation and off-design constraints, while the absolute economic values remain case-dependent.

title: Infoergy equation: A case study on vehicle energy management technology
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: “Infoergy” is not a typo, but rather the energization of information, which is an abbreviation for “information-energy”. Vehicle energy-saving is progressively evolving toward intelligent energy management systems that integrate information interaction; however, there remains a lack of quantitative description of the coupling relationship between information quantity and energy consumption. This hinders the full utilization of information to uncover energy-saving potential in energy management decisions and prevents an objective assessment of information's contribution to enhancing system energy efficiency. Therefore, this study proposes for the first time an information-energy equation that describes the intrinsic connection between information and energy in vehicle energy management technology. Aiming at the comprehensive information representation of multi-source time-varying information within the context of vehicle energy management, this equation defines vehicle velocity as the observable random variable of working condition information to quantify its uncertainty. An energy-saving potential evaluation system is then established. Then, by utilizing information metrics and energy-saving indicators to construct a nonlinear mapping model, it reveals the impact of working condition complexity on energy consumption from the perspective of information. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed infoergy equation exhibits excellent fitting accuracy and generalization capability. It effectively reproduces energy consumption trends and possesses good physical interpretability. At the application level, compared to other methods, the new paradigm of information-energy coupling mechanisms demonstrates better energy-saving effects. It provides a novel theoretical foundation and precise quantitative tools for unlocking energy-saving potential in intelligent energy management, laying the groundwork for deep energy savings in intelligent transportation systems.

title: State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries from random local charging fragments: A reliability-aware local-global fusion framework
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate battery health estimation from incomplete and irregular charging records remains challenging because local fragments differ not only in length but also in diagnostic quality. This study interprets random local charging fragments as reliability-varying partial health observations and develops RLCF-Net, which fuses local Q V response, masked voltage-location context, and scalar operating conditions. A training-only multi-evidence procedure selects a coverage-stable mother voltage interval, while category-level empirical reliability is defined as the inverse calibration RMSE for each span-region category and used for prediction-level aggregation. The framework is evaluated on two laboratory datasets comprising 121 NCA/NCM cells and a field dataset from 20 commercial EVs. On the main NCA dataset, validation-derived category reliability transferred strongly to held-out cells (Spearman 0.936; Pearson 0.983). Random single-fragment estimation achieved a cycle-level RMSE of 0.0082, whereas cross-fitted selection identified the 0.15 V + 0.20 V Val-K2 protocol with an RMSE of 0.003918. Across all nine K2 protocols, reliability weighting reduced RMSE in every case and remained statistically significant in seven protocols after Holm correction. Entity-level analyses further showed that Val-K2 improved all 14 held-out NCA cells relative to K1 (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.000122), RLCF-Net outperformed the strongest unified baseline in 11 of 14 cells ( p = 0.0419), and NCM reliability weighting reduced physical-cell macro RMSE from 0.002807 to 0.002258 ( p = 0.0322). The independently retrained NCM pipeline achieved a pooled Val-K2 RMSE of 0.002613. In the EV one-event evaluation, reliability-weighted K2 achieved RMSEs of 1.590 and 1.541 pp., with availabilities of 65.15% and 43.49%, respectively. Strict event-disjoint label-independence and common-all-protocol EV audits preserved the directional K2 benefit, although exact inference was limited by the four held-out vehicles. Single-thread CPU latency was 5.105 ms for K1 and 10.058 ms for K2. These results support reliability-aware aggregation for incomplete charging observations while identifying operating-condition-dependent reliability, limited fleet size, label-free adaptation, and automotive-MCU validation as remaining boundaries.
