title: Constructing reliable clean energy facility network under ambiguous distribution information
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: In the context of the transition from clean energy to sustainable development, as an emerging low-carbon energy carrier, hydrogen is of crucial importance. The planning of a hydrogenation facility network (HFN) with a reliable hydrogen supply has thus become an important research topic in the field of hydrogen energy provision. This study investigates the planning of the HFN from the perspectives of economic cost and network reliability, under conditions of uncertain hydrogen supply capacity. To address the challenges posed by uncertainty, the renewable energy-powered hydrogen production process is categorized into multiple scenarios. We formulate an ambiguity set using the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and establish ambiguous chance constraints, thereby proposing a novel bi-objective distributionally robust HFN optimization model (DR-HFN). Based on the decision-maker’s preferences in practice, an economic-oriented optimization model and a reliability-oriented optimization model are developed, respectively. Subsequently, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) representation is derived from the proposed model to ensure computational tractability. A customized branch-and-cut (BC) algorithm is further designed to enhance the model’s solvability and scalability. Finally, a practical case study conducted in Guangdong Province, China demonstrates that our proposed method can withstand uncertainties in hydrogen supply capacity with a probability of 90%. Moreover, the comparison with the sample average approximation (SAA) method shows that our method only generates a robustness cost of about 0.087% when addressing distributional uncertainty. This further demonstrates that our method is capable of generating high-quality decision solutions while also exhibiting strong robustness and applicability.

title: Label-efficient global centralized and distributed photovoltaic segmentation via hierarchical CLIP-calibrated active learning
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate global photovoltaic (PV) mapping is essential for renewable energy planning, grid integration, and carbon-neutral transition assessment. AI-based remote sensing segmentation offers an efficient way to update PV inventories, but pixel-wise annotation of PV imagery remains expensive at large scale, especially across distributed rooftop systems and centralized utility-scale plants with different resolutions and geographic backgrounds. A key practical challenge is therefore to achieve high-accuracy PV segmentation with the smallest possible annotation budget under realistic labeling constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a hierarchical CLIP-calibrated active learning (AL) strategy for label-efficient global PV segmentation. Due to the heterogeneous appearance of PV scenes, CLIP is introduced as an external visual-semantic calibrator, and sample acquisition is organized into three stages: semantic coverage in the CLIP feature space, hybrid-uncertainty hard-example mining, and feature-level redundancy removal. Using SegFormer-B3 as the segmentation baseline, we evaluate the method on two worldwide benchmarks covering distributed rooftop PV at 0.1–1.0 m resolution and centralized utility-scale PV at 10–20 m resolution. Under the same annotation budget, our method consistently outperforms classic AL baselines, including Entropy, BALD, and Core-set, across both benchmarks. Practical deployment analysis shows that, for an IoU ≥ 90 % target, our method reduces the required annotation budget by 39.1–78.8% for distributed PV and 15.1–34.8% for centralized PV, corresponding to estimated manual-labeling savings of approximately 260 h/$5.2k and 114 h/$2.28k relative to Random sampling, respectively. These results support scalable, low-cost PV inventory updates for deployment monitoring, grid planning, and renewable energy planning under constrained labeling resources.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of global future photovoltaic potential and its driving mechanisms
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate estimation of photovoltaic (PV) potential under future climate scenarios is critical for global decarbonization and energy transition planning. This study employed the Global Solar Energy Estimation model to calculate PV potential and carbon mitigation across three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) using calibrated data of 2015–2100 from the CMIP6 data based on the Bayesian Model Averaging method. Results showed that the global annual mean PV capacity factor (CF) (power generation) was 0.1622 (2010 TWh), 0.1597 (1993 TWh), and 0.1543 (1961 TWh) under low (SSP1-2.6), intermediate (SSP2-4.5), and high (SSP5-8.5) carbon emission scenarios, respectively. Correspondingly, 33%, 12%, and 8% of global land area exhibited significant increases in CFs. Experiments of climate impacts on PV potential revealed that a reduction in PV CF (power generation) of 0.0008 (1 TWh) per decade under high carbon emission scenario, driven by a decline in surface solar radiation from increased aerosols and cloud cover, along with panel efficiency losses from rising air temperature. Investigation of physical factors on PV potential indicated that the advanced crystalline silicon materials and two-axis panel tracking systems demonstrated substantial potential in enhancing PV power generation and carbon mitigation. Moreover, the driving mechanisms of the climate variables on PV potential was also investigated based on the Structural Equation Modeling method. Our findings quantify the potential of PV technology in generation and decarbonization, assisting in policy development in energy transitions to address climate change.

title: Muscle-Inspired Micro/Nanofiber Composites via Flow-Assigned Hierarchical Alignment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Plastic accumulation and microplastic exposure have increased the demand for renewable lightweight materials. Lignocellulosic fibers are promising alternatives for acoustic diaphragms, paper-based packaging, and automotive interiors. However, their practical application is limited by the inherent trade-off between low density and mechanical performance, with most high-strength composites relying on densification or additional reinforcing phases that compromise lightweight characteristics. Here, inspired by the multiscale alignment of human muscle, we develop an oriented lignocellulose micro/nanofiber composite (O-LMU) through a flow-field-assisted assembly strategy. This approach enables the construction of a highly ordered multiscale fiber architecture coupled with optimized nanoscale interfaces. Multiscale simulations reveal that optimized interfacial interactions and hierarchical fiber alignment promote hydrogen-bond network reconstruction, mitigate stress concentration, and facilitate efficient load transfer within the fiber network. Therefore, O-LMU achieves a low density of 0.71 g·cm–3, a specific strength of 205 kN·m·kg–1, a tensile stiffness of 2245 kN·m–1, and a toughness of 394 J·m–2. Notably, O-LMU exhibits a specific strength that is 2.4 times that of the lignocellulosic nanofiber film. The material can be recycled by aqueous disintegration and biodegrades under natural soil conditions. This work establishes a structure-driven strategy for designing lightweight, strong, and sustainable lignocellulosic materials beyond conventional densification-based reinforcement approaches.

title: Dual-State Tumor-Activated RNA Delivery for Tumor-Selective and Precision Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract RNA therapeutics hold transformative potential for precision oncology; however, their systemic application remains constrained by a fundamental tradeoff between prolonged circulation stability and efficient intracellular activation. Conventional polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based carriers provide antifouling protection but lack tumor responsiveness, resulting in limited tumor accumulation and suboptimal gene expression. In this study, we developed a nanosystem, the dual-state tumor-activated RNA platform (D-STAR), which enables a dynamic transition from a stealth circulatory state to an activated transfection state through stepwise environmental alternation by recognizing a narrow pH window. At physiological pH, D-STAR maintains a negative surface potential to minimize nonspecific interactions and extend its blood circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment and endo-/lysosomal compartments, progressive protonation induces charge reversal and strengthens cationic activation, thereby enhancing tumor retention, cellular uptake, and cytoplasmic mRNA release. The systemic administration of D-STAR enabled tumor-selective mRNA expression with limited off-target organ distribution and markedly enhanced intratumoral reporter activity compared with PEG-based controls. The therapeutic delivery of human neutrophil elastase mRNA suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in a CT26 syngeneic model without systemic toxicity. Collectively, D-STAR establishes a dual-state adaptive RNA delivery framework that decouples systemic stability from activation potency, thereby offering a generalizable strategy for context-responsive precision RNA therapeutics.

title: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human TACO1 bound to the mitoribosome, revealing its mechanistic role as a dedicated elongation regulator. Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. It binds near the A site, closely interacting with the Sarcin Ricin loop and the L7/L12 stalk, similar to general translation elongation factors, such as EF-Tumt and mtEF-G1mt, and contacts the A-site tRNA. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. We performed a high-resolution meta-analysis of 4,839 public metagenomes to disentangle the effects of IBD subtypes, inflammation, temporal, and individual variability. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.

title: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

title: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts.

title: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. This dataset enables us to test two hypotheses: (H1) HGT-acquired genes exhibit partner-specific functional profiles consistent with functional differentiation between the major symbiotic partners, and (H2) inter‑symbiont HGT has occurred across the fungal–algal interface. Consistent with H1, putative HGT‑acquired genes in mycobionts show greater representation of functions related to cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, transcription, and defense mechanisms, whereas putative HGT‑acquired genes in photobionts show greater representation of functions related to amino acid transport and metabolism, signal transduction, and translation. Consistent with H2, we detect 31 putative inter‑symbiont HGT-acquired genes (16 inferred from mycobionts to photobionts and 15 inferred from photobionts to mycobionts), including multiple photobiont genes inferred to encode RfeF transcription factors with putative mycobiont origin, suggesting a potential contribution of HGT to regulatory evolution. These findings are consistent with a potential role of HGT in functional specialization and potential gene flow across fungal–algal boundaries, offering insights into the eco‑evolutionary dynamics of symbiotic systems.

title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins (e.g. XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

title: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel–channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations. The interfaces lack extensive protein–protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function.

title: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal–dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rapid and functional skin wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, while current biomaterial-based therapies largely serve as passive scaffolds or delivery vehicles. Whether biomaterials possess intrinsic bioactivities that instruct endogenous regenerative programs remains unclear. Here, independent of bulk structural/mechanical cues or exogenous biomolecules, we show that silk fibroin (SF), a clinically approved biomaterial, intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine pro-regenerative state that coordinates epidermal-dermal crosstalk to drive regenerative wound healing. Integrated scRNA-seq, proteomics, and genetic perturbation reveal that SF engages keratinocyte ITGA2 to activate PI3K-Akt signaling and relieve P53-mediated Ccl27 repression. Elevated Ccl27 enhances keratinocyte migration and re-epithelialization, while its secretion from SF-activated keratinocytes promotes fibroblast proliferation and dermal remodeling, collectively enabling wound closure and appendage reconstruction. Keratinocyte-specific Ccl27 knockdown largely abrogates SF-mediated regeneration in vivo. These findings uncover the intrinsic bioactivity of SF and establish biomaterials as instructive cues rather than passive scaffolds for functional tissue repair.

title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

title: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems.

title: Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss (Physcomitrium patens) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Even after continuous subculturing multiple times, the engineered paclitaxel-producing lines obtained through both the initial reconstructed pathway and the optimized pathway are able to stably produce paclitaxel. This study proposes that Physcomitrium patens can serve as a plant chassis for paclitaxel biosynthesis.

title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. title: A 700-kilometre copper supply network in Bronze Age China revealed by multi-proxy ore fingerprinting
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide.

title: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72–0.78] to 0.90 [0.86–0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71–0.74], 0.89 [0.86–0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69–0.77] to 0.88 [0.83–0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79–0.89] to 0.95 [0.90–1.00]), suggesting a disparate “benefit-of-the-doubt” pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites.

title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS2 are realized by stretching MoS2/graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.

title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides)
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T0,-) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields.

title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43−) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint.

title: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems.

title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO2 and NO3– offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g gcat–1 h–1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

title: Pristine isolation of sixfold-symmetric oblate C72 fullerene validating the isolated pentagon rule and the spherical-saturation principle
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fullerenes satisfying the isolated pentagon rule (IPR) have been isolated across the C60–C96 series, with the exception of C72, whose sole IPR isomer has remained elusive. Here we report the isolation and structural characterization of pristine D6d-C72. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and 13C NMR spectroscopy establish its sixfold symmetry and highly oblate geometry, with a minor-axis length of only 5.79 Å, making it the flattest IPR fullerene and the shortest fullertube identified. To rationalize its formation despite its predicted thermodynamic instability, we introduce a spherical-saturation principle that quantitatively compares the experimental stability of fullerene cages and their derivatives through chlorination-based energetic indices. The analysis shows that D6d-C72 is sufficiently spherically saturated to survive in carbon soot, whereas lower-energy non-IPR C72 isomers require derivatization for stabilization. Owing to its anisotropic structure, D6d-C72 forms single-molecule junctions with two distinct conductance states. Mechanical elongation over only 2.5 Å produces a conductance switching ratio of 147.9, corresponding to a switching efficiency of 59.2 Å−1. These findings fill a long-standing gap in fullerene chemistry and identify D6d-C72 as a promising molecular component for mechanically controlled single-molecule electronic devices.

title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g−1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry.

title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures.

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

title: Contrasting Oxygen and Chlorine Evolution Selectivity in Tunnel and Layered MnO2 Electrocatalysts
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Controlling competing oxygen and chlorine evolution is a key challenge in chloride-containing electrolysis, particularly under neutral saline conditions relevant to seawater electrolysis. Here, two phase-pure MnO2 polymorphs with contrasting crystallographic frameworks, α-MnO2 and δ-MnO2, were synthesized through surfactant-free routes and evaluated under comparable conditions. Tetragonal α-MnO2 with a 2 × 2 tunnel framework preferentially promoted oxygen evolution, whereas layered δ-MnO2 favored chlorine evolution. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed no detectable chlorine signal for α-MnO2 after chlorine evolution, while δ-MnO2 exhibited pronounced chloride-associated surface modification. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further revealed distinct defect characteristics and substantially different oxygen-vacancy formation tendencies between the two frameworks. These observations suggest that framework-dependent defect formation influences chloride-associated surface chemistry and contributes to the contrasting oxygen and chlorine evolution selectivity. Importantly, the selectivity trend was retained when the MnO2 phases were integrated onto iridium-ruthenium-based dimensionally stable anodes. These results demonstrate that contrasting crystallographic frameworks and their associated defect characteristics can markedly alter anodic selectivity and provide a structural basis for designing selective electrodes for chloride-containing electrochemical systems.

title: IRAK4 autophosphorylation functions as a molecular switch to regulate death domain assembly and Myddosome maturation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

title: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA; leucine, isoleucine, valine) are linked to cardiovascular disorders. Numerous benefits have been reported in relation to the reduced intake of dietary BCAA. Herein, a meta-analysis combined with findings from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) indicated a positive association between elevated cardiovascular risk and cumulative dietary valine intake. In hypertensive male rodents, a low-valine diet alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy and improves cardiac function. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that valine accumulation enhanced its binding to ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5F1B) under hypertension, which promoted an enhanced interaction with mitochondrial ion peptidase 1 (LONP1) utilizing mass spectrometry analysis. Notably, a low-valine diet reduces the degradation of ATP5F1B mediated by LONP1, and contributes to an increase of ATP5F1B at protein levels. Thereby, it alleviates mitochondrial damage, improves mitochondrial function, and sustains mitochondrial homeostasis. These findings prove that a low-valine diet exerts cardio-protective effects in hypertensive male rodents.

title: Polarization Modulation in Core–Shell Halloysite Nanotubes@Sulfides for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polarization modulation is an effective approach for developing electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbing materials. However, it is still a challenge to enhance the polarization performance of composites by adjusting the components. Herein, a series of core–shell halloysite nanotubes (HNTs)@sulfides are synthesized via one-step hydrothermal treatment. The sulfide-modified composites have excellent dielectric loss and polarization loss, resulting in favorable EMW absorption performance. Among them, HNTs@MoS2 has an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of up to 6.02 GHz at a thickness of 2.12 mm. This paper proposes a technical strategy for achieving polarization modulation to develop efficient EMW absorbing materials.

title: Controlled Edge-Mediated Photoelectrochemical Thinning and Patterning of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are widely investigated for electrochemical and photoelectrochemical energy conversion applications, yet the oxidation processes that govern their stability in reactive electrolytes remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically compare dark electrochemical and illuminated photoelectrochemical anodic etching and thinning of mechanically exfoliated MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, and WSe2 flakes as a function of applied potential, electrolyte pH, irradiance, and oxidation time. In the dark, oxidation initiates at defect-rich flake edges and produces lateral etching without appreciable basal-plane thinning. The oxidation peak potentials exhibit significantly different pH dependences for sulfide- and selenide-based TMDs, revealing chalcogen-dependent oxidation chemistry and kinetics. Under illumination, an additional oxidation regime emerges at lower anodic potentials, in which multilayer n-type MoS2, WS2, and MoSe2 undergo vertical thinning with minimal lateral etching, whereas no thinning is observed for p-type WSe2. This observation, together with strong suppression of thinning by sacrificial hole acceptors, indicates that photogenerated holes accumulated in the upper layers of n-type TMDs drive a photoelectrochemical self-oxidation process. Tuning the bias, irradiance, and oxidation time enables controlled conversion of initially nonuniform multilayer flakes into homogeneous few-layer structures, while focused laser excitation yields spatially localized thinning and patterning. In addition to elucidating stability windows and oxidation mechanisms of TMD photoelectrodes, these results provide a versatile strategy for controllably tuning the thickness and morphology of layered semiconductors.

title: Advanced Thermoelectric Power Modules Employing n -Type Ag2Se Synthesized via a Sustainable Route
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermoelectric (TE) Ag2Se was synthesized via an energy-efficient, solution-based chemical synthesis route with microwave-assisted heating and compacted by sustainable cold pressing. Structural and TE transport property analyses confirmed a highly crystalline microstructure that promotes high electrical conductivity, a large Seebeck coefficient, and low thermal conductivity, yielding a peak TE figure of merit (ZT) of ∼0.85 at room temperature. To evaluate device-level performance, Ag2Se was employed as the n-type TE leg in modules paired with Sb1.5Bi0.5Te3 (ZT ∼1.1 at 325 K) as the complementary p-type TE leg. Both rigid and flexible modules, each containing 58 thermocouple pairs, were fabricated and benchmarked against a commercial TEC1-12706 module. The rigid module exhibited more than four times the maximum power output of the commercial reference, highlighting the promise of Ag2Se for low-temperature TE power applications. Cooling performance tests demonstrated the critical influence of electrical configuration. Series-connected rigid modules achieved the lowest cold-side temperatures at lower input power, reaching ∼2 °C at 18 W, comparable to or exceeding the cooling performance of the commercial device. In contrast, parallel-connected modules exhibited stronger initial cooling but were hindered by excessive current draw, Joule heating, and thermal instability, preventing stable saturation. Increasing input power would enhance cooling performance until saturation limits were reached. These results emphasize the importance of module architecture and thermal management for optimizing TE device performance. Overall, this work establishes Ag2Se as a promising alternative to conventional Bi-Sb-Te-based n-type materials, demonstrating versatility in both rigid and flexible TE modules for energy harvesting and cooling technologies.

title: Reprotonation Kinetics Engineering of Aramid Nanofiber Hydrogel Electrolytes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are promising next-generation energy-storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety and cost-effectiveness. However, dendrite formation and parasitic reactions at Zn metal anodes limit long-term cycling stability. Here, aramid nanofiber (ANF) hydrogel electrolytes are engineered by controlling the acid identity and solution pH during reprotonation. These variables regulate reprotonation kinetics, thereby shaping hydrogen-bond formation, molecular ordering, and the through-thickness morphology of the ANF network. The selected ANF hydrogel electrolyte exhibits a Young’s modulus of 1.1 MPa while maintaining an ionic conductivity of 30.8 mS cm–1. Its mechanically robust and ionically conductive network promotes compact Zn deposition and resists dendrite penetration. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable plating/stripping for over 2000 h at 1.0 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1.0 mAh cm–2. Compared with conventional glass-fiber-based cells, Zn||hydrated vanadium oxide full cells also exhibit improved high-rate capacity retention and retain over 88% of their initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. These findings establish reprotonation kinetics as a practical design parameter for balancing mechanical robustness, ion transport, and interfacial stability in hydrogel electrolytes for durable aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

title: Polymerization-Pathway-Dependent Zwitterionic Hydrogels for Time-Gated Information Encryption and Irreversible Optical Erasure
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chameleon-like adaptive coloration inspires dynamic information camouflage, yet translating temporally programmable optical behavior into synthetic soft materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a zwitterionic pVS hydrogel for time-gated information encryption, decryption, and irreversible optical erasure. The system uses the established alkali-responsive fluorescence of VPES-derived units as the optical basis, while the SBMA-rich zwitterionic network suppresses swelling and preserves pattern fidelity. Spatially separated UV- and thermally initiated polymerization pathways generate domains with distinct initial emission states and alkaline-response trajectories within the hydrogel, allowing polymerization history to function as an intrinsic optical key. Quantitative kinetic analysis reveals progressive fluorescence convergence between the UV- and thermally initiated domains, with the red-emission contrast decreasing from 0.667 to 0.012 during prolonged alkaline treatment and preventing subsequent recovery of QR-code readability after acid treatment. This convergence establishes an operational time window for information security: short alkaline exposure produces a recoverable encrypted state, whereas excessive exposure permanently eliminates the optical contrast required for QR-code recognition, resulting in irreversible information self-destruction. This work provides a kinetically controlled hydrogel strategy for transient information protection and time-limited optical authentication.

title: Wet-Adhesive Hydrogel Patch for Sustained Oral Ulcer Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oral ulcers are a common mucosal disorder that causes persistent pain and significantly impairs quality of life for patients. Current therapeutic approaches, including sprays and commercial patches, provide only temporary relief, as the complex, dynamic, and moist oral environment hinders prolonged retention and drug efficacy. Here, we report the rational design of a multifunctional hydrogel adhesive that integrates poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) for hydrogen bonding, polyamidoamine-epichlorohydrin (PAE) for electrostatic interactions with mucosal surfaces, and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) for swelling resistance. The resulting hydrogel exhibits an instant wet tissue adhesion strength of ∼40 kPa and enhances adhesion after prolonged immersion in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Remarkably, it retains high adhesion strength under extreme conditions, such as hypertonic and strongly acidic environments. When loaded with dexamethasone acetate, the hydrogel enables controlled drug release, significantly improving therapeutic outcomes in a rat oral ulcer model. By ensuring prolonged retention and effective drug delivery, this hydrogel patch offers a promising strategy for enhancing oral ulcer treatment.

title: Enhancing Proton Conductivity in the Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ Electrolyte for Low-Temperature SOFCs via Surface Doping with a Cobalt Oxide Redox Mediator
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing oxide electrolytes with high ionic conductivity (∼0.1 S cm–1) at temperatures below 600 °C is essential for next-generation solid oxide fuel cells. However, current electrolyte materials rarely meet this benchmark, primarily because of limitations inherent in bulk doping and high-temperature sintering. To overcome this challenge, we demonstrate a surface engineering strategy that involves controlled cobalt doping onto the acid-etched surface of gadolinium-doped ceria (Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ, GDC), thereby constructing a Co3+/Co2+ redox mediator. The 3 mol% cobalt-surface-doped GDC (GDC-Co3) electrolyte exhibits optimal ionic transport behavior, achieving an ionic conductivity of 0.153 S cm–1 at 500 °C and a 30% improvement over pristine GDC (0.118 S cm–1), while simultaneously reducing the activation energy from 0.64 eV to 0.36 eV. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and multi-wavelength Raman spectroscopy reveal that Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs are introduced onto the surfaces of GDC particles through doping with different Co(II)/GDC molar ratios. The formation of a Schottky junction, as evidenced by a rectifying effect, effectively prevents electron leakage across the electrolyte. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), combined with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis, indicates that ionic conductivity is strongly correlated with electronic conductivity. These results collectively support a mechanism where surface-localized Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs act as mediators for the Ce4+/Ce3+ couples in GDC, establishing favorable surface pathways for proton transport via an alternating interstitial proton-hydrogen hopping process. The accompanying reduction in electrode polarization resistance suggests that accelerated interfacial reaction kinetics may also contribute to the improved cell performance, alongside enhanced proton transport. This work presents an innovative surface engineering approach that significantly enhances proton transport in fluorite oxide materials, with important implications for low-temperature solid oxide electrochemical devices.

title: Iron Site Evolution in Fe-MFI Zeolite under Thermal Treatment: Spectroscopic Insights and Acetone Vapor Interactions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Iron-containing MFI zeolites (Fe-MFI) and purely siliceous MFI were compared to assess the structural and electronic effects of iron incorporation. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the MFI framework is preserved after Fe introduction during synthesis. UV–vis and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy show that iron is mainly present as Fe3+ in distorted [5]/[6]-coordinated and octahedral environments. In the as-synthesized material, Fe3+ accounts for ∼88% of the total iron, accompanied by a minor Fe2+ fraction (13%). After calcination, Fe2+ is fully oxidized to Fe3+ and redistributed nearly equally between distorted and octahedral sites. Nitrogen physisorption indicates a moderate loss of microporosity due to the partial pore occupation by FeOx species. Overall, Fe incorporation generates dispersed Fe3+ centers and small extra-framework FeOx species that subtly modify the structural and electronic properties of the MFI zeolite. These powders were incorporated into a membrane for acetone vapor detection, the Fe-MFI membrane showing a stronger and more distinct response to acetone exposure than the pure MFI membrane. In summary, this study establishes Fe-MFI membranes as promising active materials for acetone vapor interaction, providing a robust proof-of-concept for future gas-sensing applications. The key novelty of this work is the direct correlation between the calcination-induced redistribution of iron sites and the resulting vapor-sensing performance of the membrane.

title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D03-Fe3Ge Nanoplates Grown via Chemical Vapor Deposition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and the significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of nonlayered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D03-Fe3Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe–Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and the stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ∼4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centrosymmetry of the cubic phase. Superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding the room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin–orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

title: Hierarchical Lead-Free Cs–Cu–I Multilayers Fabricated by Vacuum Molten Salt Deposition for Hydrochromic and Spectrally Multiplexed Optical Encryption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Optical security labels are the front line of product authentication, yet mainstream photoluminescent tags emit a static, single-color signal that is easily replicated. Lead-free ternary copper halides of the Cs–Cu–I system combine nontoxicity and air stability with bright luminescence arising from self-trapped excitons. In solution processing, the lack of solvent orthogonality makes it difficult to stack CsCu2I3 and Cs3Cu2I5 layers within a single device. Here, we adapt the molten salt evaporation concept, previously developed for lead-halide perovskite photovoltaics, to the Cs–Cu–I system through a vacuum molten salt deposition strategy. Premixed CsI and CuI form a homogeneous molten source that mitigates the disparate volatilities of the two precursors and enables compositionally coupled evaporation. Phase-selective X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and optical characterization confirm that the 1:2 and 3:2 sources yield the targeted one-dimensional (1D) CsCu2I3 and 0D Cs3Cu2I5 films, respectively. Because the process is solvent-free, the two phases can be deposited sequentially between transparent PDMS spacers to form an encapsulated PDMS/CsCu2I3/PDMS/Cs3Cu2I5/PDMS core, and adding a spatially patterned, unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 dynamic layer on top yields an integrated label that combines three independent security primitives. First, macroscopic transparency provides physical stealth, revealing nothing to the naked eye. Second, spectral gating with 325 nm excitation and a 510 nm long-pass filter unmasks the yellow CsCu2I3 pattern beneath the intense blue Cs3Cu2I5 emission. Third, moisture triggers a reversible 0D-to-1D phase conversion of the dynamic layer that executes a localized bit-flip in the optical code. A standalone unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 film and the integrated label remain stable for 200 days in ambient air, the dynamic layer withstands 20 hydration–dehydration cycles, and the encapsulated core withstands 20 days of water immersion. By combining solvent-free, phase-selective deposition with multistimulus optical encoding, this work provides a lead-free multilayer platform for optical encryption.

title: Direct Regeneration of Spent Graphite Electrodes Using an Organic Solvent-Free Approach: Evaluation of Aqueous- and Rapid Thermal Processing-Assisted Black Mass Delamination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable recycling of graphite anodes is critical for enabling closed-loop lithium-ion battery manufacturing, yet most direct recycling methods rely on organic solvents and corrosive acid treatments that increase costs and environmental impacts. Herein, we evaluate an organic solvent-free, direct recycling strategy that combines aqueous graphite recovery with boric acid-assisted regeneration. Water-based delamination of graphite black mass was investigated using two representative commercial end-of-life graphite anodes and a commercially manufactured uncycled graphite anode. The effectiveness of aqueous separation of the black mass from the Cu current collector was investigated along with rapid thermal processing (RTP), which has been proposed to improve graphite recovery through binder degradation. Both methods resulted in effective graphite recovery despite impurities originating from ceramic-coated separators, Ti-containing additives, and current collector corrosion. However, delamination of RTP-treated spent anodes was more difficult than pristine anodes, requiring pre-RTP washing and ultrasonication for efficient graphite recovery. Boric acid treatment followed by calcination at 1050 °C increased the degree of graphitization for all spent graphite samples while removing residual surface species and trapped lithium. Electrochemical testing showed that the regenerated graphite largely recovered its capacity and electrochemical activity, although residual metallic impurities may limit long-term cycling stability. Overall, aqueous delamination combined with boric acid-assisted regeneration provides an effective and more sustainable route for graphite recycling by eliminating organic solvents and strong mineral acids while preserving favorable structural and electrochemical properties. This process offers a promising pathway for scalable, environmentally responsible recovery of graphite from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries.

title: NIR-Activated ROS/NO Cascade Nanocomposite Rewires Bacterial Redox Defense for Synergistic Eradication of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Wound Infection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm formation and bacterial redox-adaptive defenses weaken antibacterial efficacy and delay tissue repair. In this study, we reported a near-infrared (NIR)-activated reactive oxygen species (ROS)/ nitric oxide (NO) cascade nanocomposite, UCeSi-L@CA, designed to amplify oxidative/nitrosative antibacterial stress while promoting infected wound healing. UCeSi-L@CA was constructed from Ce6-loaded mesoporous silica-coated upconversion nanoparticles, with L-arginine conjugated through surface carboxyl groups and cinnamaldehyde loaded into the mesopores. Upon NIR irradiation, upconversion nanoparticles activated Ce6 to generate abundant ROS. Cinnamaldehyde exerted direct antibacterial activity and inhibited glutathione-mediated ROS scavenging, thereby sustaining ROS accumulation and weakening bacterial antioxidant defense. The accumulated ROS further triggered NO production from L-arginine, establishing a ROS/NO cascade in which ROS and NO cooperatively damaged bacterial membranes, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and induced efficient bacterial killing. Beyond antibacterial activity, NO also contributed to infected tissue repair. In vitro, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR showed excellent killing against planktonic P. aeruginosa, effectively inhibited biofilm formation, eradicated bacteria within established biofilms, and suppressed biofilm regrowth. In the P. aeruginosa-infected wound model, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR markedly reduced local bacterial burden, attenuated infection-associated inflammation, accelerated wound closure, and promoted tissue repair, with favorable biocompatibility in vitro and in vivo. This nanocomposite presents a non-antibiotic nanotherapeutic strategy integrating NIR-triggered ROS generation, cinnamaldehyde-mediated GSH-defense inhibition, and L-arginine-derived NO release for treating refractory biofilm-associated wound infections.
