title: Hydrophilic Zinc Metal-Organic Frameworks with Optimized Lewis Acid Centers for Enhanced Photocatalytic Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous materials for addressing water pollution challenges, owing to their tailorable structures and unique active sites. However, the regulatory role of metal centers with fully or partially filled d orbitals in interfacial behaviors during advanced oxidation processes remains insufficiently understood, posing a critical barrier to the development of efficient decontamination systems. In this study, we rationally designed and fabricated a series of MOF materials featuring ordered π-conjugated skeletons. These MOFs were constructed using 2-aminoterephthalic acid as the ligand, incorporating diverse metal nodes (Zn, Ti, and Co), and engineering hydrophilic or hydrophobic channels. The tetracycline (TC) degradation efficiencies of these MOFs under visible-light irradiation were systematically compared. By correlating the degradation results with structural characteristics elucidated via X-ray diffraction (XRD), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), combined with photoelectrochemical measurements, the influence of different metal centers on charge separation efficiency was comprehensively evaluated. The findings reveal that the Zn-MOF exhibits exceptional photocatalytic performance, which originates from the closed-shell d10 electronic configuration of Zn2+. This unique electronic structure confines electrons within the organic linker, effectively suppressing the recombination of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. Furthermore, the incorporation of Zn2+ centers prolongs the lifetime of photoexcited electrons and optimizes the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) process, thereby significantly enhancing photocatalytic activity. Radical trapping experiments identified superoxide radicals (•O2−), photogenerated electrons (e−), and holes (h+) as the dominant reactive species involved in the TC degradation process. This work highlights the potential of water-stable MOFs with suppressed charge recombination for applications in various photochemical processes beyond water treatment.

title: Molecular Functionalization Tunes Twist Angles of MoS2 Moiré Superlattices for Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In the quest for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates without noble metals, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as an important class of alternatives. In this regard, molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)-based SERS substrates have been extensively studied; however, their moiré superlattices (with controlled twist angles) could be potent candidates for significant signal enhancement. Here, we employed a molecular functionalization method using 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) as a linker to tune the twist angles of MoS2 moiré superlattices. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Raman spectroscopy experiments confirmed the formation of moiré patterns in 4-ATP functionalized MoS2 (4ATP-MoS2), with reduced twist angles in contrast to pristine MoS2 superlattices. Furthermore, we used 4ATP-MoS2 moiré superlattices as SERS substrates to probe molecules, such as rhodamine 6G, rhodamine B, methylene blue, and crystal violet. We observed significant enhancement of Raman signal intensity (on the order of 105) for all the molecules. Interestingly, pristine MoS2 did not show any significant enhancements of the SERS signals. We attribute the enhancement to the moiré interface-induced charge transfer from MoS2 to the probe molecules through 4-ATP, thereby increasing the Raman signals. This strategy could open possibilities to design moiré superlattices for improved SERS substrates and light–matter interactions.

title: Interface Engineering of Hydrated Tungsten Oxide via Carbon Nitride for Durable Electrochromic Energy Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic smart windows demand high optical contrast, fast switching, long-term durability, and charge-storage functionality, yet hydrated tungsten oxides suffer from restricted ion transport and structural degradation during repeated ion insertion/extraction. Here, we present a carbon nitride-driven phase transformation strategy for a durable energy-storing electrochromic hydrated tungsten oxide. Under mild hydrogen annealing, orthorhombic WO3·H2O nanoplates containing an optimized 10 wt % carbon nitride (CNx) selectively transform into predominantly hexagonal WO3·0.33H2O nanorods (∼80%), accompanied by a relatively minor orthorhombic fraction (∼20%). The CNx promotes structural rearrangement while providing nitrogen-rich Li+-interactive sites that regulate interfacial ion transport and improve electrochemical reversibility. Supported by density functional theory, impedance, diffusion, and postcycling analyses, the optimized WHX-CNx10% film shows favorable Li+ insertion, improved charge-transfer kinetics, and excellent structural retention. The air spray-coated film in 3-electrode system delivers 57% optical modulation at 650 nm, coloration/bleaching times of 2.9/0.6 s, stable cycling over 20,000 cycles, and an areal capacitance of 16.9 mF/cm2. A 5 × 5 cm2 device further exhibits optical modulation of 52% at 650 nm with a coloration efficiency of ∼156 cm2/C. These results establish CNx-mediated phase and interface engineering as an effective route toward scalable, durable, and energy-storing electrochromic smart windows.

title: Roll-to-Roll Fabrication of Large-Area Electrochromic WO3 Films via Slot-Die Coating and Intense Pulsed Light Processing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic tungsten oxide (WO3) films are promising candidates for flexible smart window applications. However, realizing large-area WO3-based electrochromic devices fabricated by low-temperature solution processing remains challenging. Here, we report a roll-to-roll (R2R)-compatible strategy for the fast fabrication of electrochromic WO3 films by synergistically combining an ultrafast intense pulsed light (IPL) process with trace Pt additives acting as light absorbers. Pt-incorporated WO3 (WO3-Pt) films were coated onto flexible substrates and subsequently treated within 10 ms using intense broadband irradiation from a xenon flash lamp. Structural, optical and chemical analyses indicate that the IPL process promotes the photothermal modification of WO3, while the Pt additive significantly enhances photothermal heating efficiency and electronic conductivity of the WO3 films. When integrated into electrochromic devices, the IPL-treated WO3-Pt (WO3-Pt-IPL) films exhibit high optical contrast, accelerated switching kinetics, and enhanced cycling stability compared to bare and IPL-treated WO3 films without Pt. The electrochromic device based on WO3-Pt-IPL film exhibited the highest optical contrast of 61.5% at 550 nm and a coloration efficiency (CE) of 139 cm2 C–1, whereas the devices based on bare WO3, WO3-Pt, and WO3-IPL films showed lower optical contrast values of 55.5%, 59.7%, and 59.3%, respectively, with CE values of around 80 cm2 C–1. In addition, the WO3-Pt-IPL device maintained nearly constant bleached and colored transmittance over 1500 cycles, demonstrating markedly improved cycling stability compared with the other device configurations. We further demonstrate large-area fabrication of WO3 films via R2R slot-die coating combined with IPL processing, achieving excellent spatial uniformity. This approach enables energy-efficient and scalable production of flexible metal oxide films and provides a feasible pathway for tuning charge transport and electrochromic properties in electrochromic materials.

title: Harnessing a Light-Activated Ruthenium(II) Complex Self-Delivery Nanoplatform for Tumor–Organelle Cascade-Targeted Immunotherapy via Type II Immunogenic Cell Death
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Immunogenic cell death (ICD) converts immunosuppressive “cold” tumors into immunogenic “hot” ones, yet ICD inducers with precise tumor–organelle cascade targeting and spatiotemporal controllability remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a self-delivery nanoplatform (ER-Ru NPs) constructed via the self-assembly of well-defined tumor–endoplasmic reticulum (ER) cascade-targeting ruthenium(II) complexes. The intrinsic amphiphilicity enables self-assembly of the ruthenium(II) complexes into stabilized nanoparticles with efficient tumor accumulation properties via biotin-mediated active targeting, without any exogenous carriers. Following cellular internalization, the released ruthenium(II) complex monomer specifically accumulates in the ER to generate a cleaved Ru–H2O anticancer agent and in situ reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon red-light irradiation. The robust ROS burst triggers severe ER stress via activation of the PERK/eIF2α pathway, leading to the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and the type II ICD induction. Notably, this cascade-targeted ICD activation strategy enhances not only tumor specificity but also the immunogenicity of dying tumor cells, achieving effective primary tumor ablation in the 4T1 models and simultaneously suppressing distant tumors through dendritic cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell infiltration, and memory T-cell generation. This study offers a paradigm for photoactivatable, self-delivery ICD inducers with cascade targeting, holding substantial promise for clinical translation in precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Self-assembled Carbon Nanotube/Extracellular Matrix Hydrogel as a Promising Matrix for Organoid Growth and Functional Maturation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organoids are three-dimensional, self-organized structures derived from tissue-specific cells that recapitulate key architectural and functional features of native tissues in vitro. Current organoid culture systems primarily rely on tumor-derived Matrigel, which suffers from batch-to-batch variability, high cost, and safety concerns, thereby limiting reproducibility and clinical translation. Notably, existing natural and synthetic polymeric hydrogels have not simultaneously supported efficient organoid formation and functional maturation comparable to Matrigel. Here, we present an improved composite hydrogel composed of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and porcine small intestinal submucosa extracellular matrix (SIS-ECM) as a versatile and biologically active promising alternative matrix for organoid culture. We demonstrate its broad applicability by successfully culturing adult stem cell-derived mouse intestinal organoids (mIOs), human intestinal organoids (hIOs), and human embryonic stem cell-derived vascular organoids (hVOs). Organoids grown within the CNT-SIS-ECM hydrogel exhibited formation efficiency, structural integrity, and functional maturation comparable to, and in certain aspects exceeding, those cultured in Matrigel, underscoring their advantages for transplantation-oriented applications. Mechanistic investigations revealed that CNT incorporation provides instructive bioactive cues that promote organoid development, including upregulation of high mobility group box 1 (Hmgb1), which enhances mIO proliferation and differentiation. Additionally, CNTs augment the WNT signaling pathway, thereby facilitating hVO growth and vascular maturation. Together, these findings establish the CNT/SIS-ECM composite hydrogel as a promising matrix alternative that supports organoid formation and maturation across multiple lineages, offering a practical platform for organoid-based research and tissue regeneration.

title: Manipulation of the Nanoarchitecture of Porous Media Determines Water Mobility: NMR Experiments using Metal–Organic Framework (MOF)-Functionalized Track-Etched Solid-State Nanochannels (SSNs)
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transport in hierarchically porous membranes depends on pore organization at the mesoscale, yet how this organization shapes local dynamics remains poorly understood. Herein, we employ single-sided nuclear magnetic resonance (SS-NMR) to probe the in situ diffusion dynamics of water within solid-state nanochannels (SSNs) functionalized with UiO-66 metal–organic framework (MOF). We systematically compare two distinct synthetic protocols: a one-pot (OP) interfacial growth and a counter-diffusion (CD) method. By deconvoluting the NMR signal attenuation, we isolate a minor slow diffusion component corresponding to intraparticle micropores and a dominant fast diffusion component representing interparticle constructional porosity. Our results show that OP growth produces large particle agglomerates and poorly connected pores with narrow bottlenecks, forcing water along highly tortuous paths. Furthermore, leveraging the pH-responsive surface charge of UiO-66, we find that water mobility in the well-connected CD nanoarchitecture varies measurably with pH, consistent with a surface-charge effect, whereas OP membranes show a weaker, nonmonotonic variation, consistent with dominant geometric obstruction. These findings link nanochannel architecture directly to local water mobility and identify constructional porosity as a structural parameter to consider in MOF-based nanofluidic membranes.

title: Sequential-Photocuring-Assisted Transformation of Planar Multilayer Structures into Curved Geometries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The integration of functional electronic structures into curved geometries remains challenging, as conventional approaches rely on post-shaping or adhesive-assisted assembly that separate structure formation from shape definition. Here, we present a sequential-photocuring-assisted fabrication strategy that transforms planar multilayer structures into curved forms within a single material system. A wavelength-selective acrylate–epoxy resin is designed to create a deformable intermediate state under visible light, followed by a fixation-enabled final state through UV-triggered curing. A gradient-like curing strategy, involving time-dependent evolution of conversion during sequential irradiation, allows controlled partial epoxy conversion and provides both processability and subsequent reactivity. The second curing step induces simultaneous interfacial bonding and structural stiffening, enabling adhesive-free integration and fixation of the mold-imposed geometry. A multilayer patch antenna operating at 28 GHz is fabricated and transformed from planar to curved geometry while maintaining its performance. This approach provides a material-based framework for integrating planar-fabricated structures into three-dimensional form factors without thermoforming or adhesives.

title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia–reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood–brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

title: Sporoderm-Removed Particles Enhance Oxaliplatin Immunochemotherapy against Colorectal Cancer and Mitigate Neurotoxicity via Dual-Directional PINK1/Parkin Mitophagy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a widely used and effective first-line chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal cancer. However, its therapeutic benefits are often constrained by limited antitumor immune activation and dose-limiting peripheral neurotoxicity. Here, we report that sporoderm-removed particles from Ganoderma lucidum spores (RGLS), a naturally derived bioactive particulate system, orchestrate bidirectional regulation of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy to simultaneously enhance OXA efficacy and mitigate neurotoxicity. Sporoderm removal remodeled the particle biointerface, improved the hydrophilicity of RGLS, and facilitated the release of bioactive constituents in gastrointestinal fluids, thereby increasing their bioavailability. In tumor tissues, RGLS cooperated with OXA to intensify mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive mitophagy, leading to increased tumor cell death and amplified immunogenic cell death, as indicated by enhanced calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. This immunogenic remodeling promoted dendritic cell maturation, increased intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and attenuated OXA-induced PD-L1 upregulation, collectively converting immune-cold tumors into immune-hot phenotypes. In contrast, in dorsal root ganglia, RGLS restored OXA-impaired PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitochondrial quality control, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species accumulation, and protected neurons from chemotherapy-induced injury, thereby alleviating peripheral neuropathy. These findings establish sporoderm removal as a biointerface-modulation strategy for transforming Ganoderma lucidum spores into multifunctional therapeutic particles and highlight RGLS as a promising adjuvant platform to improve the therapeutic index of OXA-based colorectal cancer chemotherapy.

title: Pendant Engineering of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocatalytic Hydroperoxide Production
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted much attention for their potential in photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. However, traditional COFs often suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics and a lack of highly electron-localized sites for O2 adsorption, leading to inefficient photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report a pore-channel electronic engineering strategy that introduces highly electron-localized cores into the pore channels of COFs by the regulation of heterocyclic pendants. The cores located in the channel of COFs acted as electron-rich active sites, enabling enhanced charge separation for photocatalytic H2O2 production. The polar furan groups were introduced onto the cores, further forming a powerful built-in electric field and hydrogen bond network within the channels, thereby accelerating the transport of electrons and protons. The furan-grafted COF (O-COF) showed a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 15,378 µmol h–1 g–1, with a yield 1.5–2.4 times higher than that of its counterparts. This work provides a valuable reference for the precise electronic regulation of pore channels in COFs to enhance photocatalytic performances.

title: Ionic-Liquid-Based Engineering of MOF Membranes: Tuning from H2- to CO2-Selective
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Reprogramming the transport preference of crystalline membranes offers a useful strategy for adapting a single membrane platform to different gas-separation tasks. Herein, we report ionic liquid (IL) engineering of pure ZIF-8 membranes to switch H2/CO2 transport from H2- to CO2-preferential behavior. A continuous ZIF-8 membrane was first fabricated on an anodic aluminum oxide support by cathodic deposition, followed by the loading of an IL of type 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]). The compact, well-intergrown, and crystalline ZIF-8 membrane was preserved after IL incorporation, and vibrational spectroscopy provided evidence for molecular interactions between confined [BMIM][TFSI] and the ZIF-8 framework. Gas-permeation measurements revealed that increasing IL loading decreased both H2 and CO2 permeances, indicating an increased transport resistance caused by partial pore occupation. However, the H2 permeance decreased significantly more rapidly than the CO2 permeance. The H2/CO2 selectivity decreased from 3.6 for the pristine ZIF-8 membrane to approximately 0.3 at 15 vol % ionic-liquid loading, corresponding to a CO2/H2 selectivity close to 3. The separation reversal originates from the combined effects of IL-induced pore narrowing and preferential CO2 affinity. This work demonstrates that confined ILs can reprogram adsorption–diffusion coupling in MOF membranes and provides a route toward process-adaptive gas-separation membranes.

title: Enhanced Reliability and Neuromorphic Functionality of a-IGZO-Based Memristors via N2 Annealing-Induced Vacancy Modulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Amorphous indium–gallium–zinc oxide (a-IGZO)-based memristors have attracted considerable attention for neuromorphic computing applications owing to their structural uniformity, amorphous-phase stability, CMOS compatibility, and oxygen-vacancy-mediated resistive switching characteristics. However, uncontrolled oxygen-vacancy concentrations can lead to unstable charge transport and switching variability, limiting reliable device operation. In this work, post-deposition N2 annealing was employed to regulate the oxygen-vacancy-related defect states of Pd/HfO2/a-IGZO/HfO2/Pd memristors. The a-IGZO layer was annealed in an N2 atmosphere at 300–600 °C, and the resulting changes in material properties, resistive switching behavior, and synaptic characteristics were systematically investigated. XPS and XRD analyses indicated that N2 annealing decreased the relative oxygen-deficient/defect-related O 1s component while maintaining the amorphous nature of the a-IGZO layer. Among the investigated conditions, the 500 °C-annealed device exhibited the most stable switching behavior, with reduced variation, improved retention and endurance characteristics, and reliable analog conductance modulation. Conduction mechanism analysis revealed that the optimized device maintained stable space-charge-limited current conduction, whereas excessive vacancy reduction at 600 °C promoted a premature transition toward the trap-filled-limit regime, resulting in degraded switching stability. Furthermore, the optimized device successfully emulated long-term potentiation/depression and paired-pulse facilitation, and its measured synaptic characteristics were validated through ANN-based MNIST pattern recognition and PPF-driven neuron circuit simulation. These results demonstrate that N2 annealing-induced oxygen-vacancy engineering is an effective strategy for improving the reliability and neuromorphic applicability of a-IGZO memristors.

title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

title: La Doping Imparts Bifunctional Interfacial Catalysis for Dehydrolactonization of 1,6-Hexanediol
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The dehydrolactonization of 1,6-hexanediol (1,6-HDO) to ε-caprolactone (ε-CL) requires a catalyst capable of cooperatively catalyzing two distinct half-reactions, namely dehydrogenation and cyclization. However, conventional catalysts lack the electronically asymmetric sites needed to drive both steps efficiently. Herein, a bifunctional Cu+–Ov–Ce3+ interfacial frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) is constructed by loading Cu onto La doping CeO2. La doping introduces additional oxygen vacancies (Ov) and Ce3+ species, thereby enriching the Ov–Ce3+ sites. Systematic characterizations (XPS, EPR, XAS, TPD, in situ FTIR) combined with DFT calculations reveal that Cu+ sites are responsible for α-H elimination to form 6-hydroxyhexanal (6-HA), whereas the cyclization reaction is driven by the FLP composed of Ov–Ce3+ and adjacent lattice oxygen. La incorporation lowers the energy barrier and enhances FLP formation. Under optimized conditions (3 wt % La, 280 °C, weight hourly space velocity of 1.5 h–1), a ε-CL yield of 61.17% is achieved with good stability over 120 h. From these findings, the interfacial bifunctional mechanism is clearly elucidated, and a defect engineering strategy for decoupling interfacial components is demonstrated, providing a rational approach to the design of multifunctional catalysts for tandem reactions.

title: Efficient Chemical Synthesis and Enzymatic Replication of 3′-Deoxyapionucleic Acid (ApioNA): An RNA-Selective XNA with Conformational Flexibility
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.

title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species
                    1–3
                    , yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in
                    Caenorhabditis elegans
                    . Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

abstract: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.

title: Biodegradable Capacitive‐Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive‐coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo‐wire interconnects, and a textile‐reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio‐NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery‐free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB‐mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro‐regenerative immune modulation, calcium‐related signaling, AMPK‐associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB‐enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic‐monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint
                    1–3
                    . Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in
                    TP53-
                    mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in
                    TP53-
                    wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex–cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/C
                    CDH1
                    ). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (
                    FZR1
                    ) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21
                    Cip1/Kip1
                    and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/C
                    CDH1
                    or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

title: Magneto‐Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical‐Mn/N‐doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time‐resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near‐complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au‐micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N‐doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO 4 •‒ ‐mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate‐determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale‐up conditions, with a machine learning model ( R 2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno‐economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value‐added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.

title: Sugar-Based 1-Dimensional Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates with Hydration-Tunable Chiroptical Emission
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral topology in semiconductors introduces a structural degree of freedom for tuning the chiroptical, excitonic, and spintronic behavior. In metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas) semiconductors, how ligand stereochemistry and supramolecular organization influence chiral topology, and thus optical and excitonic responses, remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in sugar-based 1-dimensional MOChas, with structures solved via small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography. These materials exhibit blue and green CPLs, arising from the chiral inorganic core. Despite the close chemical similarity between the glucose- and galactose-derived ligands, we observed dramatic differences in their inorganic structure. Silver glucosethiolate shows reversible hydration-driven photoluminescence switching with a hydration-linked emission energy. Labile water molecules in the glucose-based system correlate with a blueshift in excitonic emission. Our results suggest a new direction in the search for chirophotonic hybrid semiconductors, exploiting intrinsically chiral topologies and excitonic optical frequencies, which are sensitively modulated by ligand identity and supramolecular interactions.

title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Thin Film Solar Cells
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.

title: Facet-directed hydroxyl-rich surface environments stabilize iridium single atoms for efficient acidic water oxidation
source: Energy & Environmental Science
abstract: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

title: High‐Entropy Materials as a Design Paradigm for Low‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na + transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub‐zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High‐entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na + migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid–electrolyte interphase and cathode–electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy–percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade‐offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high‐entropy strategies into robust LT‐SIB operation.

title: Triboelectric DC generation via dielectric polarization coupling for self-powered IoT systems

title: Industry‐Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET‐Cu Current Collectors
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al 2 O 3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min −1 , substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al 2 O 3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al 2 O 3 ‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al 2 O 3 ‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.

title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Temperature is a fundamental parameter in reaction kinetics, typically accelerating rates according to the Arrhenius law. In catalytic systems, however, competing pathways often respond differently to temperature, allowing the selective promotion of desired reactions while suppressing undesired ones through temperature modulation. Here we show that regulating the temperature near the freezing point of water can resolve the activity-stability trade-off in the oxygen evolution reaction on manganese dioxide. Although lowering the temperature decreases water oxidation rates, catalyst degradation through permanganate formation is suppressed more effectively, extending catalyst lifetime. Counterintuitively, further cooling below 0 °C accelerates permanganate formation, yielding an optimum temperature near 0 °C that balances activity and stability. This anti-Arrhenius behaviour, arising from electrolyte supercooling, is a rare example of anomalous temperature-dependent electrocatalysis under subzero conditions. Our findings highlight temperature regulation as a viable strategy for enhancing catalytic lifetime, with implications for electrochemical systems operating in wintertime and in polar and extraterrestrial environments.

title: Integrated soft robot capable of surviving extreme underwater shock loads
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Soft robots have been developed for underwater tasks owing to their compliant, damage-tolerant bodies, which foster an expectation that soft bodies are inherently robust in aquatic environments. However, most reported systems operate under moderate or quasi-static conditions, and overlook a critical vulnerability—when cavity-rich soft structures are subjected to underwater shocks, the embedded cavities collapse violently, triggering a phenomenon we term ‘soft-matter implosion’. This process generates internal pressures several times higher than the incident pressure and can severely damage onboard electronics. Using a simplified cavity-containing structure, we combine underwater impact experiments and finite element simulations to reveal the mechanism of soft-matter implosion and quantify the peak pressure under different parameters. These results inform a function-structure co-design framework that suppresses implosion while preserving overall flexibility. Guided by this framework, we built a rigid-casing-free, fully integrated manta‑ray‑inspired soft robot that survives single impacts up to 49.8 MPa and sequential impacts at 31.5 MPa, and resumes flapping locomotion after impact. This work establishes an impact‑resistant soft robot platform and provides a generalizable design strategy for durable, flexible machines operating in challenging underwater environments.

title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored
                    1,2
                    . Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems
                    1–3
                    . Some commercially available compostable plastics
                    4–7
                    , developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited
                    8–10
                    . Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-
                    co
                    -adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-
                    co
                    -terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2–6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution.

title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems
                    1–5
                    . However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation
                    1–5
                    , rising tree mortality
                    6–8
                    and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest
                    9–11
                    . Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions
                    1–4,11,12
                    . Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable
                    1,9,13
                    . Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts
                    9,14–17
                    . Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO
                    2
                    measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr
                    −1
                    , with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr
                    −1
                    ) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011–2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr
                    −1
                    ) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019–2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr
                    −1
                    ) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr
                    −1
                    ) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.
